title: Performance Marketer (m/w/d) - Meta Ads × AI × Creative Strategy | E-Commerce, Online Marketing
description_clean:
Die meisten Performance Marketer können eines von dreien. Wir suchen jemanden, der alle drei verbindet.

Wenn du verstehst, warum das richtig sein kann, bist du hier richtig.
Zweitens: AI - richtig eingesetzt. Wir sind eine AI-native Agentur. Das heißt bei uns: eigene MCP-Anbindung an die Ad-Accounts, automatisierte Audits und Anomalie-Erkennung, selbstgebaute Skills für Angle-Entwicklung und Skript-Bau. Diese Werkzeuge sollst du nicht bedienen wie ein Formular, sondern führen wie ein Instrument: AI übernimmt das Wie (Analysen strukturieren, Varianten bauen, Daten durchkämmen), die Hypothese - das Was - bleibt deine. Drittens: Creative Strategy. Bei High-AOV entscheidet das Creative, nicht der Kampagnen-Setup-Trick. Du musst keine Creatives produzieren, aber du musst sie lesen können: Warum gewinnt dieser Winner? Welches Segment, welche Kaufhürde, welcher Beweis fehlt im Funnel? Du entwickelst mit dem Creative-Team Hypothesen (Segment → Mechanismus → Angle), verstehst, warum ein kalter Markt andere Hooks braucht als ein heißer, und liest Creative-Performance jenseits von Hook Rate und Thumbstop.

Unsere Kunden kaufen Urteilsvermögen, kein Button-Pushing: dass wir ihr Geschäft verstehen - Marge, Customer Journey, Liquidität - und nicht nur Anzeigen ins System tippen.
Aufgaben

Du führst Accounts end-to-end: Audit → Hypothese → Test-Plan → Skalierung → Reporting.
Du steuerst nach Total Business Numbers und inkrementellen KPIs; du verstehst warum Last-Click bei langen Journeys täuscht.

description_clean: Angefangen hat alles vor sieben Jahren als ambitionierte Idee. Heute sind wir Marktführer für Abschlusszeitungen in Deutschland. title: Internship or Working Student Position – Learning Management & Innovation (all genders)
description_clean:
Job summary
Join our Transformation team, where you’ll be fully integrated from day one. 
In the Transformation team we work towards the vision of unleashing everyone’s full innovation potential at Lufthansa Group and beyond. We equip employees and leaders with the mindset and skillset for driving digital innovation and transfer the methodologies, culture, and structures we see at innovative companies into the corporate context. For that, our team built a portfolio of products and tailored formats to upskill Lufthansa Group employees and leaders on topics like digitalization (especially AI), innovation, technology, and cultural transformation. 
As an Intern (full-time) or Working Student (>20h/week) in the Transformation team, you will support the design, marketing, and delivery of our formats – from innovation trainings and workshops to community events and thought leadership content. Many of these formats take place at our office in Berlin-Mitte, where you’ll help create a unique customer experience and take charge of event hosting with service excellence in mind. 
You’ll collaborate closely with a multidisciplinary team to connect people, ideas, and technologies that shape the future of Lufthansa Group. 
The position is located in Berlin with occasional onsite presence at the Lufthansa Group locations in Frankfurt am Main, Munich, Hamburg, and Cologne. 
Start: asap
Stellenbeschreibung
Responsibilities

Support the planning, marketing, design, and facilitation of (virtual) workshops, learning formats, and events for Lufthansa Group employees.
Research and create engaging content around innovation for our learning formats as well as our communication channels (e.g. internal channels, Miro boards, knowledge management pages, mailings).
Create a unique customer experience by organizing and hosting training days end to end, from venue setup, catering and logistics to participant communication, ensuring service excellence at every touchpoint.
Scout new exciting (LearnTech) technologies as well as relevant trends and translate them into trainings, workshops, and projects.
Take ownership of small projects and continuously improve our team processes, e.g. by exploring AI trends and applying them to increase efficiency.

Anforderungsprofil
Profile

Student in an education-/psychology, innovation-, entrepreneurship-, design/media-oriented orcommunication-related field.
Strong communication skills in German and English and a confident presence.
You’re passionate and curious about rethinking learning, with a stake for what makes good learning formats work and what keeps participants engaged. Experience in Learning & Development, training, event management, corporate innovation, consulting or startups is a bonus.
Curiosity and strong research skills for topics like digital transformation, innovation culture, and AI & emerging technologies.
Enthusiasm for actively using AI in everyday work and experimenting with new use cases – first experience in building small automations or skills is a plus.
Familiarity with tools like Miro, Mailchimp, Notion, Canva, Figma, MS Teams, or AI tools (e.g. Claude) is a plus.
High degree of motivation, self-initiative, ownership, strong organizational skills and a passion for hosting people.

Was wir bieten
What we offer

Be part of a diverse, forward-thinking team shaping the innovation agenda of Lufthansa Group.
Gain hands-on experience in learning and transformation projects and exposure to senior leadership.
Work in a collaborative, growth-oriented environment that values experimentation, ownership, and personal growth.
Develop your facilitation and innovation skills in the heart of the Berlin tech ecosystem.
Experience the value of cross-functional collaboration acrossleaning,innovation, design, and strategy.
Corporate benefits: A USC membership – and yes, we also do have a fruit basket.

About us
At Lufthansa Innovation Hub, we accelerate the NEXT in travel. Founded in Berlin over a decade ago, we bring together entrepreneurial minds and jointly lead progress in shaping the future of the travel industry. By continuously expanding our footprint in the ecosystem, we actively shape industry conversations and secure valuable partnerships and innovation opportunities. 
The NEXT in travel is built today: With focus, ambition, and purpose, we develop solutions to drive and enable (y)our innovation agenda.

title: Customer Success / Operations Architect (m/w/d)
description_clean: Über BirdsviewBirdsview ist die Agentic Sales Platform für den E-Commerce: KI-Agenten, die autonom verkaufen - per E-Mail und direkt im Shop. Vor allem dort, wo Kataloge komplex sind und gute Beratung den Unterschied macht.Das Fundament ist die Birdsview Intelligence: eine Wissensschicht, die Sprachmodellen echte Retail-Verkaufsexpertise gibt. Sie versteht Kundenlebenszyklen (Lifecycle IQ), Produkte und wie sie zusammenpassen (Product IQ), Produktbilder (Vision IQ) und die Tonalität jeder Marke (Emotional IQ) — modellagnostisch und direkt auf den Daten des Shops.Darauf arbeiten unsere Sales Agents:Avys verkauft per E-Mail: Sie schreibt jedem Kunden eine individuelle Mail, wählt Produkte und Zeitpunkt, trifft den Ton der Marke und versendet selbst — ohne Flows, Segmente oder Agentur.Robyn verkauft im Shop: Sie bringt dieselben Empfehlungen direkt auf die Produktseiten — über dasselbe Plugin, ohne neue Integration.Unsere Kunden - Online-Händler und Marken auf Shopware und Shopify, von LUSH über TeeGschwendner bis Egle - wechseln zu uns, weil unsere Agents sofort live sind, im Schnitt ein Vielfaches ihrer Kosten einspielen und 1:1-Personalisierung at scale liefern, während Incumbents wie Klaviyo manuelle Tools bleiben, die meist eine Agentur zum Betrieb brauchen.Deine MissionDie Rolle in einem Satz: Du bist das Gesicht von Birdsview für unsere Kunden, von Go-Live bis Renewal, und baust gleichzeitig die AI-Systeme, mit denen das ohne Ticket-Flut skaliert.Wir suchen keinen klassischen Customer Success Manager, der Tickets abarbeitet. Unser zweiköpfiges Customer-Team betreut unsere Kunden bereits jeden Tag — was fehlt, ist das System dahinter: klare Prozesse, Automatisierung, ein durchgängiger Weg vom Vertragsabschluss bis zum Renewal. Mit den beiden arbeitest du jeden Tag eng zusammen, und genauso eng mit den Foundern: Ihr sitzt zusammen im Office, stimmt Prioritäten direkt ab, und du bekommst ungefilterten Einblick in Produkt, Vertrieb und Strategie.Du übernimmst die End-to-End-Verantwortung für Ergebnisse und Systeme in diesem Bereich: Du bringst Kunden live auf Avys und Robyn, machst sie messbar erfolgreich, verantwortest Renewals & Expansion — und baust den Bereich so um, wie ein AI-Unternehmen ihn heute bauen sollte: automatisiert, skalierbar, AI-first. Am Ende beantwortet kein Mensch mehr First-Level-Anfragen — nicht, weil wir am Team sparen, sondern damit Menschen bei uns nur das tun, was Maschinen nicht können: Beziehungen, Eskalationen, Wachstum.Das erwartet dichGo-Live: Du onboardest neue Kunden auf unsere Agents — vom Kickoff über die Shop-Anbindung (Shopware/Shopify) bis zur ersten Mail von Avys und den ersten Empfehlungen von Robyn im Shop.Success: Du bleibst nah an unseren Kunden, machst den ROI unserer Agents sichtbar und sorgst dafür, dass aus Go-Lives begeisterte Referenzen werden.Growth: Du verantwortest Vertragsverlängerungen und Upsells auf neue Features und Produktlinien.Systeme statt Tickets: Du baust den Customer-Bereich AI-first um — automatisiertes Onboarding, Health Scores, Self-Service, AI-gestützter Support (n8n, Claude, APIs). Ziel: Repetitive Anfragen erledigt die Maschine, dein Team hat den Rücken frei für alles, was echten Impact hat.Voice of the Customer: Du ownst Eskalationen und übersetzt Kundenfeedback in Produktentscheidungen — mit direktem Draht zu Engineering und Foundern.Was du mitbringen solltestDrive, Lernwille, Smartness: Das zählt für uns mehr als Jahre im Lebenslauf. Customer-Success-Erfahrung brauchst du nicht unbedingt — du kannst auch direkt nach dem Studium einsteigen. Die Founder arbeiten eng mit dir und bringen dich schnell auf Tempo.People Person: Du hast echtes Interesse an Customer Success und an den Menschen hinter unseren Kunden. Du suchst den direkten Kontakt, am Telefon, im Call oder vor Ort, baust Vertrauen auf und machst Kunden zu Partnern.Systems Thinking: Du automatisierst dich selbst aus repetitiver Arbeit heraus, bevor jemand danach fragt.AI-native: LLMs sind dein Tagesgeschäft, du baust Workflows mit n8n, Make & Co., nutzt Tools wie Claude Cowork aktiv und hast keine Berührungsängste mit APIs und Webhooks.Commercial Edge: Du willst Umsatzverantwortung übernehmen und scheust keine Renewal- oder Pricing-Gespräche.Work EthicVelocity > Komfort: Du liebst es, wenn Dinge schnell passieren.Ownership: Du übernimmst Verantwortung und lieferst Ergebnisse.Figure-it-out-Mentality: Viele Prozesse existieren noch nicht — du baust sie.Hard Work / High Reward: Du verstehst, dass ein Early-Stage-Startup kein 9-to-5 ist.Deine ersten 90 TageMonat 1: Du kennst jeden Kunden, das Team und jeden bestehenden Prozess — und dessen Lücken.Monat 2: Die drei größten manuellen Prozesse laufen automatisiert.Monat 3: Dein Renewal- und Expansion-Playbook steht, und du präsentierst das Operating System für Customer @ Birdsview.Was du bekommstAttraktives Gehalt + VSOPDirekter Impact auf Umsatz und ProduktEnge Zusammenarbeit mit den Foundern: kurze Wege, schnelle Entscheidungen, steile LernkurveHardware deiner Wahl, flexible Arbeitszeiten, 30 Tage UrlaubBedingungenStandort: Düsseldorf/Köln — Hybrid möglich, aber mehrere Tage unter der Woche im Office in DUS (bei den Foundern)Start: ASAPFind more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

Our signature product, neos™, is the world’s first non-invasive neuro-ophthalmoscope for fast, automated assessment of eye movements and pupils. Founded at the University Hospital of Bern, Switzerland, we’ve grown into a startup of 25 engineers, clinicians, scientists, and specialists working side by side. We aim to bring the diagnostic quality of highly trained specialists into secondary and primary care settings everywhere.The RoleYou’ll help us understand how neos™ behaves when its components work together—and where they fail. description_clean:
Functie  Reliability engineer
 
Beschrijving functie
 
De reliability engineer is een productie specialist die de totale levensduur van installatie bestudeert en analyseert hoe het bedrijf omgaat met investeringen en onderhoud van assets.  De reliability engineer is de expert in het identificeren van potentiële risico’s en het voorkomen van stilstanden. Daar problemen moeilijk volledig te voorkomen zijn, geeft de reliability engineer adviezen hoe te handelen bij storingen die plaatsvinden. Het doel is te voorkomen dat fouten in productiesystemen optreden.
 
De reliability engineer analyseert tevens de veiligheidsrisico’s geassocieerd met installatie fouten. Ter voorkoming van stilstand maakt de reliability engineer onderhoudsschema’s en analyseert statistische gegevens die helpen te voorspellen wanneer en hoe fouten voor kunnen komen. De reliability engineer ontwikkelt inspectie criteria die gebruikt worden om de asset health te monitoren. 
Om dit te kunnen bereiken maakt de reliability engineer gebruik van een aantal technieken.
 


Voorlopige gevaren analyse: Preliminary hazard analysis is de initiële identificatie van potentiële gevaren en fouten in een productie proces of systeem


Failure modes and effect analysis ( FMEA): Betreft het opsommen van de manieren dat een proces of systeem kan falen en wat de consequenties hiervan zijn.


Criticality analysis: bepaalt hoe ernstig de consequenties zijn van een asset fout voor het productiesysteem van het bedrijf.


Onderhoudbaarheid: gedetailleerde informatie hoe efficiënt en betrouwbaar het bedrijf een onderdeel kan repareren.


Foutenboom analyse: onderzoek van een systeem fout door naar de kleinere voorafgaande gebeurtenissen te kijken die hebben bijgedragen aan de systeem fout

title: Werkstudent:in Community Management (m/w/d)
description_clean:
1KOMMA5°
Bei 1KOMMA5° verfolgen wir eine Vision: Living on wind and sunlight forever for free. Dafür bauen wir mit Heartbeat AI das Energiesystem der Zukunft. Bist du dabei?Wir bringen regionales Handwerk und skalierbare Software zusammen: Solar, Speicher, Wärmepumpe und E-Mobilität denken wir nicht einzeln, sondern steuern sie als intelligentes, integriertes Gesamtsystem in unserem virtuellen Kraftwerk. Direkt verbunden mit dem Strommarkt – in Echtzeit, vollautomatisiert. So wird Energie dann genutzt, wenn sie erneuerbar verfügbar und besonders günstig ist. Bis 2030 wollen wir 1,5 Millionen Haushalte auf erneuerbare Energien umstellen. Über 3.000 Menschen arbeiten jeden Tag daran, an mehr als 80 Standorten weltweit, von Finnland bis Australien.   
Du willst Verantwortung übernehmen und Lösungen bauen, die wirklich zählen? Bewirb dich jetzt und gestalte mit uns die Energiewelt von morgen.
Deine Position
Ob in den Kommentaren unserer Social-Media-Kanäle oder in Bewertungen auf Trustpilot und Google – überall dort entsteht ein Stück öffentliches Bild von 1KOMMA5°. Damit wir dort schnell, passend und im Sinne unserer Marke reagieren, suchen wir dich als Verstärkung für unser Community- und Bewertungsmanagement – mit Gespür für Sprache, Plattformen und den Menschen dahinter.
Community Management & Bewertungsmanagement (dein Hauptfokus)

Du unterstützt das Team bei der Community-Betreuung auf Instagram, Facebook, YouTube und LinkedIn in der zeitnahen Beantwortung von Kommentaren und Nachrichten im Ton von 1KOMMA5°
Du unterstützt im operativen Bewertungsmanagement: Du screenst neue Bewertungen auf Trustpilot und Google, reportest Auffälligkeiten und hilfst bei der Implementierung entsprechender Maßnahmen
Du behältst wöchentlich das relevante Video-Umfeld auf YouTube im Blick, sichtest ausgewählte Kanäle und Beiträge rund um 1KOMMA5° und gibst deine Beobachtungen strukturiert ans Team weiter, damit bei Bedarf schnell die richtigen nächsten Schritte eingeleitet werden können
Du unterstüzt unsere Organic Traffic Machine: Direkt nachdem neue Inhalte auf unseren Kanälen live gehen, gehst du aktiv in die Kommentare unserer eigenen Posts, stößt Diskussionen an und sorgst so mit dafür, dass unsere Inhalte zusätzlich an Reichweite und Sichtbarkeit gewinnen
Du behältst die Logiken der einzelnen Plattformen im Blick – was auf LinkedIn funktioniert, funktioniert nicht automatisch auf Instagram – und kommunizierst dabei immer im Sinne von 1KOMMA5°
Du platzierst unsere Inhalte auch dort, wo sich Gespräche über Energiewende, PV, Wärmepumpen & Co. sowieso schon abspielen – zum Beispiel durch passende, wertstiftende Kommentare auf anderen Accounts

Dein Signature-Projekt: GEO

Du übernimmst bei uns das Thema GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) als eigenes kleines Projekt und bringst dich inhaltlich aktiv ein: Du entwickelst mit, wie unsere Social-Media- und Community-Inhalte so formuliert und aufbereitet werden, dass sie auch in KI-gestützten Suchergebnissen und Antworten gut sichtbar sind
Du bringst eigene Ideen ein, testest neue Formulierungsansätze und hilfst dabei, GEO nach und nach fest in unsere Content-Erstellung einzubauen

Dein Profil

Du bist noch mindestens zwei Semester an einer deutschen Hochschule im Bereich Marketing, Kommunikation, Medien, BW L oder in einem vergleichbaren Studiengang immatrikuliert
Du bist selbst viel auf Social Media unterwegs und verstehst intuitiv, wie sich Instagram, Facebook, YouTube und LinkedIn jeweils unterscheiden – in Ton, Format und Zielgruppe
Erste Erfahrung im Community- oder Social-Media-Management ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss – wichtiger ist uns dein Gespür für Sprache und Menschen.
Du schreibst sicher und stilsicher auf Deutsch, Englischkenntnisse sind von Vorteil
Erfahrung mit Social-Media-Management-Tools wie Agorapulse (oder vergleichbaren Tools) ist hilfreich
Ein Grundverständnis von SEO bzw. GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) ist ein Plus – vor allem aber hast du Lust, dich in dieses Thema als eigenes kleines Projekt einzuarbeiten und es aktiv mitzugestalten
Du interessierst dich für die Energiewende und hast Lust, dieses Thema jeden Tag ein Stück greifbarer zu machen

Benefits

Du hast die Möglichkeit in unserem schicken Showroom in der Hamburger Innenstadt zu arbeiten und/oder remote
Einblicke in das Community Managemen t eines der am schnellsten wachsenden CleanTech-Startups Europas
Ein Team, das dir Fragen beantwortet, Feedback gibt und dich in die Plattform- und Tool-Logiken einarbeitet
Flexible Arbeitszeiten, die sich mit deinem Studium vereinbaren lassen
Nutze dein technisches Equipment auch abseits der Arbeit in deiner Freizeit
Du bist Teil eines schnell wachsenden Unternehmens mit viel Entwicklungspotenzi al, wo du eigenständig etwas aufbauen kannst und deinen Impact spürst
Bewege dich in flachen Hierarchien, übernimm schon während deiner Einarbeitung Verantwortung und arbeite direkt mit Teilen des Managements zusammen
Mit deiner Arbeit unterstützt du den Megatrend “Energie- und Mobilitätswende” und leistest einen konkreten Beitrag zum nachhaltigen Umbau unserer Energie-Infrastruktur
Sei aktiv und nutze das Angebot von über 7.600 Sportpartnern mit dem EGYM-Wellpass

 Your main mission will be to ensure the smooth deployment and flawless execution of framework agreements (accords-cadres) and public tenders throughout their lifecycle. You will be the guarantor of compliance with public procedures and tracking commitments, acting as the primary operational point of contact for public beneficiaries and freelancers.

Onboarding & Pedagogy: Pitch platform benefits, lead training sessions, and perform product demos to drive user independence within ministries, local authorities, and public institutions.


Public Tender Execution & Tracking: Anticipate the end of purchase orders or contracts, and provide proactive follow-ups to ensure business continuity and secure renewals (contract renewals, new market lots).


Public Administrative & Budgetary Management: Pilot operational processes specific to the public sector (management and compliance of quotes/purchase orders, tracking Legal Commitments (Engagements Juridiques), validating activity reports/CRA for non-autonomous clients), and monitor budget consumption.


Beneficiary Relations & Satisfaction: Act as the dedicated go-to person to centralize requests from public decision-makers and resolve operational incidents.


Contractual Expertise (SLAs & CCAG): Master the specificities of technical/administrative specifications (CCTP, CCAP, CCAG) and service level agreements (SLAs) unique to each framework agreement to align our internal ways of working.


Continuous Improvement: Identify operational pain points unique to public administrative processes and collaborate with Ops, Product, and Tech teams to automate and adapt our platform to public sector constraints.


About you 🧑‍🚀


Experience: A previous public sector experience is mandatory for this job ! Solid background in managing complex client relationships, onboarding large accounts, or operational contract management


Administrative Rigor: A keen sense of organization and familiarity with the inner workings of public administration (notions of public procurement, purchase orders, Chorus Pro, and budgetary validation workflows).


Solution-Oriented: Excellent interpersonal skills, diplomacy, and the ability to resolve disputes or complex situations with a variety of stakeholders (from Procurement Directors to technical Project Managers).


Tools & Data: Advanced proficiency in collaborative and analytical tools (Gsheet/Excel, Notion, Looker) and an appetite for AI applications.


Languages: Native/fluent level of French (essential for dealing with the French administration) and professional level of English (as internal processes and the Malt team are international).

First call with our Talent Acquisition team to better understand your background and aspirations (30-45 minutes).

title: Product Marketing Manager (F/H)
description_clean:
At Younited, we believe credit and banking should feel as simple, fast and transparent as everything else in your digital life.
So we build financial services that way. We combine technology, data and automation to rethink the way people borrow, pay, save and manage their money.

Today, more than 1.5 million customers trust us, and nearly 500 employees contribute to our growth across 4 European countries.

What we build




Younited Credit – instant consumer credit, directly accessible to customers.


Younited Pay – instalment payment and financing solutions embedded into our partners' customer journeys.


Younited Cashback – cashback and personalised offers, enhanced by open banking data.


Younited Bank – our everyday banking offering, currently available through helios by Younited and being expanded.




Our ambition is to build a financial partner people genuinely trust, combining simplicity, transparency and responsible finance. As a certified B Corp, we integrate social and environmental considerations into the way we build our business.
 
The 5 values we work by




Make it simple - in the product, in the customer experience and in how we organise. Be transparent.


Act as an entrepreneur - take ownership, play as a team, dare to try and accept failure.


Innovate or die - challenge the status quo, however impossible it may seem.


Faster is better - speed over perfection, alignment over debate.


No limit - shoot for the moon, stay humble.




We give passionate problem-solvers the space to do their best work in diverse and inclusive teams across Europe, because that is how we build better financial products for our customers and partners.
Context 📄
How do you turn complex credit and payment products into propositions that customers understand, partners value and teams can sell?
As Product Marketing Manager at Younited, you will shape the insights, narratives and tools that help our products stand out and grow. You will work across Younited’s product portfolio, with Younited Pay as your initial priority given its strategic importance and the competitiveness of its market.
Within Marketing Central, you will join the Customer Engagement team and work with Product, Sales, Partnerships, Data, Brand & Communications and local marketing teams. Depending on business priorities, your scope may evolve across different Younited products, audiences and customer journeys.
Your mission will be to understand the audiences we want to reach, clarify what makes our products valuable and turn market, customer and field feedback into concrete recommendations for Sales, Partnerships, Product and Marketing. You will connect market reality, commercial priorities and product decisions by turning research, customer insights and field feedback into clear messages, useful tools and actionable recommendations. You will also work closely with the PRM/CRM teams to connect these insights with customer journeys, engagement and retention initiatives.
Key responsibilities 🚀
1) Build market and customer understanding


Conduct market research, competitive analysis and customer data analysis to identify target audiences, understand their needs, uncover opportunities and bring the voice of the customer into business and product decisions.


Work across several products, audiences and business priorities, with Younited Pay as the initial priority.


Work with the PRM/CRM and Customer Engagement teams on segmentation, use cases and customer journeys across acquisition, activation, repeat usage and retention, including merchant onboarding for Younited Pay and other priority journeys across the Younited portfolio.


2) Define positioning and support commercial teams


Clarify the benefits, differentiators and key messages of Younited products, making complex topics compelling and easy to understand for customers, merchants, partners and internal teams.


Turn market and customer insights into sales pitches, presentations, enablement materials, partner tools and practical recommendations that help Sales and Partnerships teams explain and sell our products.


Contribute to strategic RFPs by understanding requirements and shaping the response narrative, value proposition, differentiators, proof points and presentation materials.


3) Partner with Product teams and support product evolutions


Bring market feedback and customer insights into product discussions and roadmaps, and influence product decisions based on market and customer feedback.


Support product launches and evolutions with the necessary materials, including demos, training materials, operational guides, FAQs and sales enablement documents.


Work across Product, Sales, Partnerships, Data, Brand & Communications and local marketing teams to turn insights into clear messages, useful tools and actionable recommendations.


About you 👇


You have at least 5 years of experience in B2B Product Marketing, Product Marketing or a related role.


You know how to conduct market research, analyse competition and turn customer and market insights into clear, actionable recommendations.


You are comfortable working across several products, audiences and business priorities.


You understand Sales and Partnerships teams’ challenges and know how to create useful, practical materials that support commercial teams.


You are comfortable contributing to strategic RFPs and tailoring a value proposition to different business and partner contexts.


You are comfortable working with Product teams and influencing product decisions based on market and customer feedback.


Experience in payments, banking, credit, fintech, e-commerce or another complex or regulated industry is a plus.


You know how to make complex topics simple and compelling, both in writing and verbally.


You are fluent in French and English.


You are autonomous, structured, proactive and able to manage several projects in parallel.


You know how to adapt your approach to different audiences and switch between strategic thinking and hands-on execution.


You know how to influence stakeholders without relying on hierarchical authority and deliver concrete results.


Hiring process 📅


First video interview with Arthur, Lead Talent Acquisition Manager, to discuss the role, your motivations and Younited.


Second interview with Lise, Head of Customer Engagement, to explore the expectations of the role in greater depth.


Business case, followed by a debrief and conversations with members of the team.


Final interview with Ricardo, Growth & Business Operations Director, to validate overall alignment with the role and potential development opportunities.

🎁 Other benefits from joining Younited ?

Offices located in the heart of Paris (9th arrondissement)
An international work environment and the opportunity to go on assignments in our offices abroad (Barcelona, Lisbon, Rome)
An entrepreneurial mindset and strong team spirit
Personalized managerial and HR support during onboarding and throughout your Younited journey
A continuous learning environment with access to internal and external training, an e-learning platform, and “Friday workshops” within the Tech team to support everyone’s development

If your answers are yes, we should talk.
At Nomagic, we are executing a humble pivot for general-purpose physical AI. We believe that physical AI is fundamentally a knowledge transfer problem - we are leveraging the "internet data" of robotics - massive deployment logs from real systems operating in production environments -  to bootstrap our efforts. Play with real robots, solving real problems, every day.
Relocation package.
Flexible working hours.
English-speaking environment.

We combine world-class research with top-notch engineering and apply it to solve real problems
The data already exists. We have robots in production at scale. We aren't waiting for datasets to be collected; the byproduct of our machines doing useful work is being created right now.
We measure what matters. We test our code in unit tests, simulations, and directly on real robots. Grounding our models in deployment allows us to truly measure performance.
High leverage, high impact. We’re still a highly focused team. If your training recipes improve our agents, you directly change the economics of the company.
World-class peers. Our team has built Google Warsaw, unicorn startups, led research in DeepMind, tested rocket engines, and worked at top companies like Nvidia and ByteDance. Now, we are shaping the reality of Physical AI together.
We are building the bridge. We aren't a new startup looking for an application; we are an established player bootstrapping physical AI. We believe that this will be the first true proof-of-concept for scaled physical AI.

What you will do
Your focus will be defined by the intersection of Robotics and ML and large-scale multimodal model training - expertise in both is optimal and alternatively eagerness to learn.
Expect challenges across two main pillars with the opportunity to specialise:

Core Research & Large-Scale Infrastructure
Own the Training Stack: Design, implement, and maintain the core infrastructure for large-scale VLA model training, including scheduling, distribution, job management, checkpointing, and rigorous logging.
Enable Rapid Iteration: Build the critical tools and abstractions necessary for launching, monitoring, debugging, and seamlessly reproducing complex, multi-variant experiments.
Train from Deployment Logs: Utilize our massive repository of offline, classical stack data to pre-train robust robot foundation models.
Drive the Software Feedback Loop: Translate core research needs into concrete infra capabilities, track experiments, analyze results, and close the loop directly with ML researchers to unblock model progress


Real-World Evaluation & Operations


Design Physical Benchmarks: Design new robotic tasks and build lightweight physical setups to systematically evaluate model capabilities far beyond the limits of simulation.
Execute Structured Evaluations: Ensure robots are properly configured, calibrated, and ready for rollouts. You will coordinate data collection efforts and run structured, on-robot evaluations to measure real-world success rates.
Close the Physical Feedback Loop: Analyze real-world evaluation results to guide the ML research direction. You will identify operational bottlenecks across software, hardware, and deployment systems to continuously improve our iteration speed.
Scale the Workflows: Beta test internal and third-party tools for teaching robots new skills, and write clear, structured documentation so the broader team can reproduce your workflows and scale your impact.


What skills we’d like you to have:


Experience: Deep experience and understanding at the intersection of machine learning, systems engineering, and robotics.


Proven Track Record: Experience training, fine-tuning, and deploying modern deep learning architectures (Transformers, VLMs or VLAs, Imitation Learning, RL) for robot control, ideally with policies validated on real hardware.


Engineering Excellence: Strong software engineering and infrastructure skills. You are highly proficient in Python and deep learning frameworks (PyTorch/JAX) and can write clean, scalable code for training and evaluation.


Robotics Intuition: Comfort working hands-on with hardware. You understand the robotics full stack (perception, controls, state estimation) and how to debug failures when software meets the physical world.


Pragmatic Research Mindset: You possess the ability to move seamlessly between research and implementation. You prefer execution, iteration speed, and real-world robustness over theoretical purity.


What should you expect once you apply?  

A phone screen with the hiring manager to discuss your background and our technical direction.
A half-day of on-sites (cultural fit & deep-dive technical interviews).
A final decision made within 2-3 days after the on-site interview.
Important: Expect detailed, honest feedback after completing the process, regardless of our decision.

title: Closer (m/f) - Investor Relations in Düsseldorf
description_clean:
Late shift. High stakes. Six US time zones. One shot per call.
This is a genuine job posting -  not a ghost job!
Let's skip the part where we tell you this is “an exciting opportunity in a dynamic environment.” You've read that sentence four hundred times and seen it all.  
Here's what's actually true:
We need an experienced, financially literate Closer who speaks English on a native or C2 Level, can pick up a phone at 3:30pm, talk to a stranger with eight figures in a brokerage account somewhere in Wyoming or Connecticut, get them to sign a convertible promissory note before their assistant walks in with coffee. That's it. That's the job. Everything else is detail.
Who We Are
Meridion AG runs the show from Monheim & Düsseldorf. Our US arm, Meridion Dynamics Inc., builds intelligent software and smart energy technology. But you're not selling the product. You're closing the investment that funds it. Different animal, different muscle.
Aufgaben
What You'll Actually Do

Take warm(ish) leads from our setters - accredited US investors who already know we called - and close them on convertible promissory notes.
Walk investors through the accreditation process without losing them to paperwork fatigue.
Hold the line, know the terms cold, and answer the “wait, what happens if you don't hit your IPO timeline” question without blinking.
If a setter is running low on appointments, out sick or on vacation, you step in and run up to 100 outbound cold calls that day to convert cold leads into your Closing appointments. Yes, a hundred. We count :)
Talk to people who have people and AI to screen their calls - and get past their Gatekeepers.

Qualifikation
What You Bring

Real closing experience - several years of it, in high-ticket sales, investment products, or anything else where “no” is the opening bid, not the final answer. This is not a rookie position.
English at a genuine native level. Not “I watched a lot of Suits.” You need to sound like you belong in a room with a family office CFO. If it's not your first language, we're talking true C2, no exceptions. An accent is no Dealbreaker but your vocabulary, your pronunciation, the way you use idioms - your vibe on the phone - must be on fleek.
A voice and presence that reads as calm, unbothered, and confident - think less “modern hustle culture” - more Brian Tracy.
Genuine understanding of what an accredited investor is, what a convertible note does, and why someone would put $50k+ into one. We'll brief you thoroughly - but you need financial literacy to keep up from day one.
A working understanding of US investor culture, even sitting in Düsseldorf’s Seestern District.

Benefits
The Deal

Full-time, 40h/week, onsite at our Düsseldorf office near Seestern. 
Late shift: 2:30pm - 10pm, because your workday runs on Pacific and Eastern time, not Berlin time.
Base salary + commission  
Onboarding is real: Expect a genuine ramp-up before you're fully solo on calls.
Start: ASAP - which translates to “realistically September/October”.

Not For You If
You cling to a script forever to feel confident. You've never been told “no” 70 times in a day and called it Tuesday. You think “Closer” means you show up after someone else already did the hard part.
Sound like your Tuesday? Send us your CV.We don’t do 5 interview rounds.You talk to me on the phone or in a brief Teams Video Call.
If I sense you’re a fit, we’ll welcome you onsite for another brief interview with our CEO; please plan in approximately 2h for the interview, a brief vibe check with the team and one or two test calls so we can hear your closing performance.  
That’s it.Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

description_clean:
Tinder exists to help people meet, connect and create a spark. After 13 years of leadership in the dating industry, culture is what keeps that mission relevant to each new generation of daters. Product is central to this shift. Every new feature is a chance to tell a human story about how people connect, and culture is where those stories land.
To make that shift real, we’re bringing our Tinder MarComms regional EMEA strategy together: one unified in-country team in each key market and one regional structure. Communications now sits within Marketing, so both work toward the same KPIs and growth objectives.
The Integrated MarComms role is where culture meets brand relevance, with one holistic objective: driving MAU growth. Social Media is the true D2C MarComms engine for Tinder, and creator and influencer led activations play a central role in driving registrations, reactivations and cultural relevance.
The regional MarComms team owns the full paid, earned and owned media cycle across key markets. The Integrated MarComms Senior Manager leads the earned and influence dimension of that ecosystem, with a strong influence on owned social channels and brand partnership storytelling.
The role reports to the Director of Marketing of France & Benelux. It works in a matrix with the Snr. Director of Social Media, Snr. Manager of Brand Partnerships, and closely with the Global Comms team.
 Key Responsibilities
1. Creator & Influencer Ecosystem Engagement

Build and nurture a diverse network of community voices: creators, influencers, podcast hosts, cultural commentators and community leaders.


Develop collaborations rooted in a strong audience insight and shared creative idea, giving partners a meaningful role beyond content distribution.


Work closely with social, influence and brand partnership teams to connect local opportunities with broader brand priorities.


Create opportunities for audiences to participate and share their own stories, turning campaigns into conversations that extend beyond launch.

2. Social-First Integrated MarComms Strategy


Translate market priorities into integrated MarComms plans for France & Benelux, in close partnership with the market lead, marketing manager and EMEA teams.


Develop compelling creative ideas with the potential to travel across paid, owned and earned channels, giving each channel a clear role in building relevance, consideration and action.

title: Director, Satellite Business International | Directeur(trice), Développement Commercial International - Satellites
CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
description_clean: The question Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards. What you will do The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request. 1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report. 2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured. 3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along. 4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFET-based analog alternative may be considered where appropriate. Jointly vary sampler steps, stochastic bitstream length and effective precision to identify an operating point predicted to yield a real energy advantage over digital CMOS at a small, tunable loss in sample quality. The result is a frontier predicted from mathematical and hardware models, then verified against calibrated measurements. A clear negative answer is more useful to us than a vague positive one: a negative result on point 3 leaves points 1 and 2 intact and turns point 4 from a prediction into a measurement.  Who we are looking for Required • A PhD in applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning, electronic engineering, computer science or a closely related field, obtained (or with the defence scheduled) before the start of the contract. • A strong foundation in probability and stochastic analysis, numerical analysis, optimisation, or machine learning: SDEs, Girsanov’s theorem, time reversal of diffusions, with the ability to apply it rigorously to diffusion or other generative models. • Familiarity with the convergence theory of sampling algorithms, or the demonstrated capacity to acquire it quickly, for example through Langevin/MCMC analysis, optimal transport or concentration of measure. • Solid scientific computing (PyTorch or JAX), and the habit of writing code others can run. Ability and motivation to work across mathematical modelling and hardware-aware AI. • Working English; French is not required. Valued, not required Prior work on diffusion or score-based generative models; numerical analysis of finite-precision arithmetic. Familiarity with hardware-aware machine learning, approximate or stochastic computing, analogue in-memory computing, device modelling, circuit simulation, photonics, ferroelectric devices, or energy modelling. Experience linking model accuracy or robustness to implementation non-idealities, such as quantisation, noise, drift, variability, finite precision, or correlated errors. Evidence of interdisciplinary research, for example work at the interface of mathematics, machine learning, devices, circuits, architectures, or electronic-design automation. No hardware experience is expected or needed to apply.What matters most We are seeking a researcher who wants to explore how to turn physical constraints into mathematical and architectural design parameters. The project does not require prior laboratory hardware experience: INL provides device expertise, measured characteristics and modelling infrastructure. However, the successful candidate must be prepared to engage critically with non-ideal analog, photonic and ferroelectric accelerators, and to work with both supervisors to connect device-level error mechanisms, score-error guarantees and the energy–quality trade-off of diffusion-model inference. Candidates with a primarily mathematical background and strong curiosity for hardware are welcome, as are candidates from AIhardware, device-modeling, circuit, architecture or EDA backgrounds who have the stochastic-analysis maturity needed to develop the theory. The decisive criterion is the ability to make the mathematics and hardware inform one another, producing predictions that are quantitative, testable and relevant to an energy-efficient accelerator demonstrator.What we offer • A real double supervision, with weekly meetings that alternate between ICJ and INL. The two laboratories are on the same campus, five minutes apart on foot. • A question publishable on both sides: mathematics journals for the theory, design and hardware venues for the co-design. • Involvement in INL’s design–technology co-optimisation work through the PEPR Électronique CHOOSE project, and contact with the group’s ferroelectric and photonic device work (FVLLMONTI, Ferro4EdgeAI). • Support for conference travel and open-access publication, funded by the two host laboratories, and the career-development measures the establishment provides for post-doctoral researchers. • Practical help for international recruits through Espace ULYS, the EURAXESS service centre for Université de Lyon: visas, housing, health cover, banking, schooling. Amine (Co-founder & CTO) is an AI researcher from École Polytechnique who worked extensively on discrete diffusion and turned down a PhD with Google DeepMind to build Davis. They started working together in July 2025 at Entrepreneur First's first European residency, a two-month lock-in in a German castle.Today we are a team of twelve: technical profiles from Polytechnique, ENS and INRIA alongside architects and deep real estate expertise. We are small with an extremely high bar. If you want to work deeply on hard problems and see your work reach clients within days, you are the one we need.Why We Will WinReal estate is a $13 trillion industry that technology has largely bypassed. The professional services that feed it (design, engineering, feasibility, permitting) represent hundreds of billions in spend that no one has seriously automated.Proptech spent the last decade selling SaaS on the edges of these workflows. Today, more than 5,000 customers, including companies like AWS, Deel, HubSpot, Clay, and Artisan, trust us to power their prospecting and enrichment.Founded in Paris and now headquartered in San Francisco, we're a team of 50+ people across the US, Europe, LATAM, and Israel, growing quickly and building with speed, ownership, and ambition. It's the system responsible for deciding which data providers to call, in what order, under which conditions, and what happens when something fails. effectively.Design scalable multi-tenant architecture: Develop the foundations for sub-accounts, customer-specific credit pools, and endpoint-level configuration, ensuring the engine remains flexible, verified regardless of their original data source.Strengthen our core architecture: Improve and refactor existing systems as we scale, applying strong engineering practices to keep our codebase clean, understandable, reliable, and easy to maintain.Shape technical decisions: Work closely with our engineering leadership to translate product requirements into thoughtful architectural solutions, balancing immediate needs with long-term scalability.What Success Looks LikeIn your first 3 months:Develop a deep understanding of our existing waterfall engine, provider integrations, and core backend architecture.Build strong relationships with the engineering team and identify opportunities to improve reliability, performance, and maintainability.Start contributing to the evolution of our routing engine, taking ownership of initial architectural improvements and technical decisions.By 6 months:Take ownership of key components of our core platform, delivering meaningful improvements to provider orchestration, fallback logic, and routing capabilities.Help introduce more flexible, account-level configuration while keeping the architecture clean, scalable, and maintainable.Improve the reliability and observability of our provider integrations, reducing operational complexity as we scale.By 12 months:Play a leading role in delivering a more intelligent, configurable waterfall engine that supports different customer needs and optimization goals at scale.Establish robust architectural foundations for multi-tenancy, composable verification, and continued provider expansion.Be a trusted technical contributor within the engineering team, helping shape long-term architectural decisions and ensuring our core platform remains reliable, performant, and ready for future growth.What title: Software Engineer Intern - Robotics Platform
description_clean:
Gravis Robotics is a high-growth Series A start-up backed by SoftBank, bringing Physical AI to the construction industry, turning heavy construction machines into autonomous robots. 
Gravis began as an ETH Zurich spin-out, and our unique combination of learning-based automation and augmented remote control lets one operator safely conduct a fleet of earthmoving machines in a gamified environment. 
Backed by deep robotics research and now deployed across multiple countries with leading construction and equipment partners, our team is rapidly growing to bring this technology to a trillion-dollar industry. 
The Gravis RACK is a machine-agnostic retrofit kit that adds autonomy to excavators and wheel loaders from 10 to 100+ tonnes: LiDAR and camera sensing, GNSS RTK, networking hardware and rugged edge compute that works offline. Paired with the Slate tablet and our Copilot software, it lets an operator run a machine manually, with AI assistance, or fully autonomously.  
About the role
At Gravis, we build high tech systems that give machine operators superhuman capabilities. To adapt in real time to changes in the environment the Gravis Rack fuses data from LiDAR, cameras, GNSS, and hydraulics into an autonomous control system. The robotics platform team builds the software foundation for our robots to enable non stop operation in the harshest environments. We ensure all algorithms execute correctly, based on a rock solid communication layer and world class introspection capabilities. We provide all the tools to deploy, develop and debug the most powerful robots on earth.
As a robotics platform software engineer intern, you will help build our vision of a scalable, safe and high performing robotics platform. You will  gather requirements from internal customers, work on communication layer, node orchestration and lifecycle management as well as APIs to off-machine systems.
What you'll do 


Design, build and maintain parts of the robotics platform, e.g. APIs, health monitoring and machine configuration management


Contributing to high quality code, improving robustness and maintainability of existing code


What we're looking for


Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field


Hands-on experience in Software Engineering


Solid Software Engineering skills


Programming skills in a systems language like C++ or Rust, Python is nice to have


Bonus qualifications 
Don't meet every requirement? We still want to hear from you. These are nice-to-haves, not dealbreakers:


Experience in computer networking


Experience in information security


Experience working with embedded systems


Experience working on production grade software system


Open source contributions



This is an opportunity to join a dynamic, multidisciplinary team and to be part of a company that is reshaping heavy construction.
Gravis is an equal opportunity employer. Trace failures through complex payment flows using logs and transaction traces, then raise clear, prioritised defects and work with engineers and external partners until they're fixed

Experience testing software both manually and with automation, including turning requirements into test scenarios and deciding what to automate first based on customer, launch and technical risk.
Ability to analyse logs, transaction traces and test results, and to write defect reports that include reproduction steps, expected versus actual behaviour, impact and evidence.
Comfort working with Git and Jira (or similar tools)

Become a Part of Accurids
Join us and help make medicinal product data useful for all!  
At Accurids, we build the data backbone behind life-science innovation. Our platform identifies, links and standardizes critical enterprise data in line with global standards such as the ISO standard for the Identification of Medicinal Products (IDMP), and some of the world's largest pharma companies use it to bring products to patients faster and more safely.  
You will join our Services department, a group of interdisciplinary experts who help our pharma customers adopt our platform and make it truly useful for their data. Within it, you are part of the data engineering team, which works in a clear, well-documented way: state-of-the-art tools, flexible processes, and agentic AI used in a structured, reliable way. You see your results in live customer projects within weeks, and learn the pharma data domain from people who have worked in it for years.  
How you’ll make an impact:

You transform data from a wide range of structured sources (such as CSV, JSON, RDF, and SQL and NoSQL databases) into the IDMP data model, and build the pipelines that keep it up to date.
You use AI to turn unstructured sources such as documents and texts into structured, verifiable data.
You bring a DevOps mindset to data: with AI as your everyday tool, used responsibly, you keep data flows and tooling tested, automated, documented and reliable, as the regulated pharma industry demands.
You support the design of data models for IDMP knowledge graphs, leveraging the IDMP ontology, and learn to navigate graphs with SPARQL and agentic tooling.
As part of a joint team with our customers, you work directly with their domain experts to understand their data and make their medicinal product data useful.

What helps you succeed:

A background in computer science, data science or a life-science subject such as biology, chemistry or pharmacy. A formal degree is welcome but not required.

description_clean: Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.Grâce à des outils de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nos enseignants-chercheurs inventent le concept de « Material by design » : concevoir les matériaux dès l’atelier de recherche, pour une performance sur-mesure.🧠 Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.🎯 Description du poste - ce que nous attendons de vousLe Laboratoire Georges Friedel (LGF) est une Unité Mixte de Recherche du CNRS (UMR 5307). Situé à l’École des Mines de Saint-Étienne et porté par deux tutelles (Mines Saint-Étienne et CNRS), le laboratoire regroupe tout le potentiel de recherche de Mines Saint-Étienne dans les domaines des matériaux, de la mécanique et des procédés.Le centre SMS - Sciences des Matériaux et des Structures - est l’un des cinq centres d’enseignement et de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne. Au sein du LGF, il développe des recherches en science des matériaux, mécanique et procédés avancés de fabrication, pour le transport et la production d'énergie, avec un objectif d’accroître la durabilité des matériaux.Ce post-doc s'inscrit dans le cadre de la chaire « SIRA », un partenariat de cinq ans entre Mines Saint-Etienne et les sociétés Framatome et EDF, co-financé par l'Agence Nationale de la Recherche, portant sur le vieillissement des aciers faiblement alliés (16MND5) utilisés dans les composants du circuit primaire des réacteurs nucléaires à eau pressurisée. Les travaux de la chaire incluent plusieurs doctorats et post-doctorats visant à faire progresser la connaissance du phénomène de ségrégation intergranulaire dans les aciers faiblement alliés et de la fragilisation associée, ainsi qu’à développer de nouvelles méthodologies de mesure de la ségrégation intergranulaire, ou à améliorer les méthodologies existantes.Le post-doc proposé ici, financé par EDF, vise à déterminer l'effet de l'irradiation neutronique sur la ségrégation intergranulaire, pour les matériaux suivis dans le cadre du programme de surveillance des effets de l'irradiation sur les matériaux des cuves REP d'EDF. Il est en effet important de savoir si de la fragilisation intergranulaire peut intervenir à forte fluence pour prévoir correctement l'évolution des propriétés de rupture. C'est donc une caractérisation qui vient en appui de l'interprétation des fragilisations mesurées dans le cadre du programme de surveillance. Le travail consistera à mesurer les états de ségrégation intergranulaire dans les états non irradié et irradié en utilisant la microscopie électronique en transmission (STEM-EDX). Contrairement à la spectroscopie Auger, la microscopie électronique ne nécessite pas l'obtention d'une surface de rupture sous ultra-vide, ce qui constitue un avantage pour des matériaux dont la tendance à la rupture intergranulaire est faible. L'acier de cuve a une certaine hétérogénéité de composition chimique locale à cause de la présence de mésoségrégations enrichies en solutés majeurs et en impuretés fragilisantes comme le phosphore. Pour juger des seuls effets de l'irradiation, les zones d'analyse en microscopie électronique devront donc être équivalentes en termes d'intensité de mésoségrégation dans les états non irradié et irradié. Ceci nécessitera une caractérisation préalable des mésoségrégations et un prélèvement ciblé des lames minces en zone ségrégée ou en zone non ségrégée par faisceau d'ions focalisés (FIB). Les travaux de microscopie électronique seront réalisés à Saint-Etienne (microscope Jeol NeoARM) pour l’état non irradié, et au laboratoire d'analyse des matériaux irradiés d'EDF à Chinon (microscope FEI Osiris) pour l’état irradié. Une méthodologie d'analyse des ségrégations intergranulaires a été développée pour ce type de microscope au cours de la thèse de C.Y. Hsu (2023) et fait actuellement l’objet d’un développement dans le cadre d’un des post-docs de la chaire (mesure de la ségrégation intergranulaire du carbone par STEM-EDX).Le poste est basé sur le campus de Saint-Étienne, avec des déplacements réguliers au LIDEC d’EDF (CNPE de Chinon, 37420 Avoine).  🔍 Ce que nous recherchonsVous êtes :· Titulaire d'un doctorat en Sciences des Matériaux ou Physique ou ChimieVous êtes doté(e) des compétences, connaissances et expériences suivantes :· Bonne connaissance de la science des matériaux· Expérience en microscopie électronique en transmission et FIBVous vous reconnaissez dans les capacités et aptitudes suivantes :· Capacité à travailler en équipe· Capacité à dialoguer avec des interlocuteurs académiques et industriels 📩 Candidatez dès maintenant !Date limite de candidature :  15/12/2026🔗 Les dossiers de candidature (CV, lettre de motivation, lettre de recommandation) sont à déposer sur la plateforme RECRUITEE : https://institutminestelecom.recruitee.com/o/post-doctorante-influence-de-lirradiation-neutronique-sur-la-segregation-intergranulaire-dans-un-acier-faiblement-allie-cdd-24-moisPrise de poste envisagée : 1er février 2027Les candidats retenus après examen de leur dossier de candidature seront auditionnés en entretien par visioconférence puis, le cas échéant, reçus pour un entretien en présentiel à Mines Saint-Étienne.Dans le cadre de sa politique Égalité, Diversité et Inclusion, l’École des Mines de Saint Etienne est un employeur soucieux de l’équité de traitement entre les candidatures. ℹ️ Informations complémentairesCDD de droit public d’une durée de 24 moisLa rémunération sera fixée selon le profil du candidat, en fonction des règles définies par le cadre de gestion de l’Institut Mines TélécomTemps pleinProfil Cadre Poste basé à Saint-Étienne à l’École des Mines. title: Software Engineer, Knowledge Engine  – Data Infrastructure
description_clean: The Knowledge Platform team builds Exa's knowledge engine. We continuously synthesize information from across the web and beyond into one of the world's largest open-domain knowledge graphs, with hundreds of billions of evidence-backed claims. Our goal is to give agents answers to any factual question about the world with unprecedented precision and completeness.In this role, you'll build the knowledge construction pipelines: turning everything from a 100k docs/s web crawl to vendor datasets into a graph of what is true about the world, and keeping it correct as data changes.This is greenfield work with a massive scope. At Airalo, we're making it easier for people to stay connected wherever they travel. As the world's first eSIM store, we help millions of travelers access affordable mobile data in 200+ countries and regions around the world.
Today, we're a team of 400+ people across 60+ countries, building a product used by travelers every day. We've grown quickly, but we've worked hard to keep what matters: trust, ownership, and the freedom for people to do great work without unnecessary layers or bureaucracy.
We're fully remote by design, genuinely global, and united by a shared mission to make travel simpler for everyone.
Your Next Destination

Location: Remote.
Contract: Full-time, permanent.
Benefits: Learn more about our benefits here in this link - https://airalo-public.notion.site/Benefits-25396a97ffca81fb9bc1f0be479f1be3?pvs=74 
Languages: English is our main working language day to day, so you'll need to be comfortable communicating in it both in meetings and async.

 

Airalo's fully remote Data team is growing, and so is our ambition for how we measure marketing. You'll help Airalo decide where to invest the next dollar by owning how we measure marketing performance: attribution, the data models behind it, and incrementality testing that shows what really works, turning evidence into investment decisions across the globe.
You'll pair solid measurement expertise, including causal inference, with strong core analytics. You'll guide teams on what to measure and test, defend our framework with senior stakeholders, and make sure data changes decisions. This is a small, growing team and a capability that is new to the business: you'll build the process, not inherit it. Expect your time to be split between measurement work (attribution, data modelling and incrementality) and the day-to-day analytics Growth and Marketing rely on.
What You'll Do

Support our marketing attribution models and methodology: review how conversions are credited across channels, reconcile platform-reported and first-party numbers, and keep the approach trusted and documented.
Design and maintain the marketing data models behind measurement (spend, attribution, orders and customer cohorts) with Analytics Engineering, with clear definitions, tests and documentation.
Support Growth and Marketing with ad-hoc and core analytics, such as campaign and market performance, self-serve dashboards and AI-assisted analytics.
Design and run geo experiments from simulation-based power analysis and market selection to success criteria and read-out, working with the marketing performance team.
Co-own a prioritised quarterly incrementality test roadmap across channels and markets, ranked by decision value, cost, feasibility (including properly powered tests) and learning, and track each test through to a decision.
Handle spillover, seasonality and small-market noise, and report incremental CAC and incremental ROAS with honest uncertainty.
Turn test results into investment guidance: estimate marginal returns and saturation by channel and market, and recommend where the next dollar should go and where to pull back.
Help set and document our causal measurement standards: which method when, what counts as sufficient evidence, and how results calibrate attribution and MMM for budget allocation.
Defend the framework under challenge from channel owners and leaders, and pressure-test platform claims.
Guide Growth, Acquisition and Finance from business question to testable hypothesis to budget decision, and build literacy on attributed versus incremental performance.
Build reusable experiment tooling and templates, work with Analytics Engineering and MarTech on the data experiments needed, and document every test and decision as you build this capability from scratch.

What You'll Bring

3+ years of experience in marketing measurement (attribution, incrementality or marketing mix modelling), with a track record of analysis that changed real budget decisions.
Solid grounding in causal inference and experimental design: randomised and quasi-experimental methods such as synthetic control and difference-in-differences, simulation-based power analysis to size and design tests, and knowing when each approach breaks.
Strong statistical judgement: you can quantify uncertainty, explain it simply, and resist overclaiming.
Hands-on experience with marketing attribution models and their limits, including reconciling platform-reported results with first-party data.
Familiarity with how experiments calibrate MMM and attribution, and with marginal-return and budget-optimisation thinking (saturation, diminishing returns).
Expert SQL and Python, production-quality code, a modern warehouse (BigQuery or Snowflake) and a BI tool such as Lightdash or Looker.
Strong data modelling skills: designing clean, tested and documented models (dbt or similar) for marketing spend, attribution and customer data, and working closely with Analytics Engineering.
Strong core analytics skills: marketing and customer metrics (CAC, LTV, retention, funnel and cohort analysis), dashboards and self-serve BI, and the judgement to prioritise ad-hoc requests alongside the test roadmap.
Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders: you hold a position under challenge, have shaped a roadmap, and say no with a clear rationale.
Comfortable with ambiguity and with data that is still improving: you're a proactive self-starter who is happy to create a new process or capability in a small, fast-growing team.

We started Airalo to make staying connected effortless, wherever you are in the world. Today, millions of travelers rely on our eSIMs, and many of the people building the product were customers first.
Our team spans 60+ countries, united by a shared belief that great work happens when people are trusted to own what they do. There's trust to own what you do, space to focus without constant layers of process, and a clear sense of what you're responsible for from day one.
As Airalo continues to grow, so do the opportunities to learn, take on new challenges, and make a real impact - from anywhere in the world.

At Opencast, we don’t measure developers by the number of tickets you complete. We care about engineering craft, clean design and thoughtful problem-solving. 
Opencast consultants deliver in complex environments, pairing often and working with others who take pride in doing things properly: TDD, emerging design, refactoring and leaving code better than they found it. We build software we are proud of, and our clients trust us not just to code but to think, challenge and guide. If you value simple and robust solutions and want a role where your judgment matters as much as your keyboard, you will fit right in.
The role
We’re looking for Contractors in Software Development (Senior level or Technical Lead) to help our major clients transform. 
Software developers at Opencast care about building products right and combine their own experience and approach with our company values. They are tech agnostic, have expertise in agile methodologies, extreme programming practices and use industry-leading programming languages to deliver agile transformation.
Our approach to software development is collaborative, focused on keeping things simple, and we use test driven development and pair programming as best practice.
Working with clients and key stakeholders is a crucial part of a consultancy role. Our developers are inclusive team players that listen, collaborate, can positively challenge and manage expectations when needed but most of all are always willing to teach and help others. Leaving a client with improved ways of working, working technology and a good experience from discovery through to live is the priority.
Contractors at Opencast follow the same principles as permanent consultants. The roles are varied, technical, and never confined to any one provider or solution.
Requirements
Due to the nature of this role, applicants must either currently hold active Security Check (SC) Clearance or be eligible to obtain it.
Eligibility typically requires UK citizenship and continuous residence in the UK for the past five years, with no single absence exceeding 28 consecutive days.
As attendance at client sites is a routine part of the role’s working pattern and involves occasional travel, travel expenses are not covered.
Experience in delivering digital services for the UK government is highly valuable for many of our projects. Therefore, familiarity with the GDS toolkit will be beneficial.
Technical Skills

Expertise in Java and/or Scala is required
Experience in other languages such as Javascript, Typescript, Kotlin, Python or Ruby is also valuable
Experience in a technical leadership role
Deep understanding of programming paradigm, code design, testing, accessibility, performance and security
Proven ability to apply different testing tools and methods in practice
Knowledge or experience of delivering complex services to Government Digital Service (GDS) standards
Being comfortable with new technology, t-shaped and comfortable with ongoing learning and development is key to success
Experience with agile methodology

A contractor in software development at Opencast is responsible for:

Driving the elaboration of their team’s backlog
Setting testing strategies to match industry standards
Being a technical expert in their team (or acting as the team lead)
Leading the technical representation in a project discovery
Acting as a technical lead in the team, enabling them to achieve their full potential
