title: AI Platform Engineer
description_clean:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AI Platform Engineer based in Germany.
Join a forward-thinking technology team building the AI platform that powers intelligent agents across multiple business functions, including engineering, business development, compliance, support, and finance. In this hands-on individual contributor role, you will design, develop, and operate the infrastructure that enables AI agents to perform increasingly autonomous tasks safely and reliably. You will work across agent runtimes, integrations, identity management, security guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and observability. Collaborating closely with internal domain experts, you will turn operational challenges into scalable AI-powered solutions that deliver measurable business value. You will take ownership from initial design and implementation through production deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement. This remote-first opportunity is ideal for an experienced engineer who combines strong software fundamentals with practical expertise in deploying and scaling LLM-based systems.
Accountabilities
You will help build and evolve the organization's AI platform, enabling teams across the business to deploy reliable, secure, and increasingly autonomous agents. Your responsibilities will include:


Productionizing AI workflows: Transform prototypes into robust production systems with defined service-level agreements (SLAs), supporting use cases such as specification-to-pull-request agents, AI-powered code reviews, incident triage, and Know Your Business (KYB) reviews.


Building and managing MCP servers: Design, deploy, secure, and maintain Model Context Protocol servers, including authentication, per-user OAuth, scoped access, and integrations with tools such as Slack, GitHub, Jira, HubSpot, and internal services.


Developing autonomous agents: Build multi-step agents capable of planning and taking action across different tools, progressing through controlled trust stages from shadowing and suggesting to executing tasks autonomously.


Implementing security and governance: Establish platform-wide guardrails, including agent identities, scoped credentials, audit logs, CI checks, approval workflows, allowlists, and least-privilege access policies.


Creating evaluation frameworks: Develop test datasets, evaluation criteria, regression suites, and live production scoring systems to measure agent quality and connect performance metrics to business outcomes.


Improving observability: Instrument agents and workflows with tracing, logging, latency and cost metrics, drift detection, alerts, and dashboards that help internal Operators monitor performance.


Managing AI expenditure: Track usage and spending across AI providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, and OpenRouter. Establish budgets, alerts, and cost attribution at the team, agent, and workflow levels.


Supporting internal stakeholders: Work directly with Operators across business functions to understand their needs, develop requested features, create documentation, deliver enablement sessions, and build self-service tools.


Developing reusable AI capabilities: Create and maintain shared skills, plugins, and knowledge resources covering company processes, standards, security requirements, and brand guidelines.


Driving process automation: Proactively identify repetitive manual workflows that could benefit from AI, implement automation solutions, measure their impact, and continuously improve them.


Taking end-to-end ownership: Write technical specifications, plan and deliver projects independently, communicate progress asynchronously, and remain accountable for monitoring and improving solutions after deployment.


Requirements
The ideal candidate combines strong software engineering fundamentals with hands-on experience building and operating production-ready AI systems. You should be comfortable working independently, communicating with technical and non-technical stakeholders, and applying sound judgment to complex automation and security challenges. Required qualifications include:


At least 5 years of experience as a software, platform, or infrastructure engineer, with a solid understanding of system design, data modeling, testing, debugging, and code review.


Between 6 and 12 months of experience shipping LLM-based systems to production and supporting agentic workflows used by real end users.


Daily, hands-on experience using AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex to write, test, and review production code.


Experience developing autonomous or multi-step agents with tool integrations, using technologies such as the Claude Agent SDK, Anthropic APIs, OpenAI APIs, or similar frameworks.


Practical experience building MCP servers, including OAuth authentication flows, scoped tokens, and user-level access controls.


Knowledge of identity and access management systems such as Okta or similar identity providers, including SSO protocols (SAML/OIDC), SCIM provisioning, group-based access, and device policies.


Experience creating automated system identities, including GitHub Apps, service accounts, API keys, and managing secrets through tools such as 1Password.


Understanding of security guardrails and governance practices, including least-privilege access, audit logging, CI checks, approval gates, allowlists, and policy-as-code.


Experience designing evaluation systems for LLM applications, including test sets, evaluation rubrics, CI regression testing, release gates, and live production scoring.


Practical experience implementing production observability through tracing, metrics, alerting, and dashboards, using tools such as OpenTelemetry, Grafana, Datadog, Langfuse, LangSmith, or Braintrust.


Experience monitoring and controlling AI expenditure across providers through API key limits, cost centers, budgets, and actionable alerts.


Strong programming skills in at least one of TypeScript, Python, or Go, alongside working knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and cloud infrastructure.


A demonstrated ability to independently identify and automate manual processes, supported by two or three concrete examples of previous work.


Strong written communication skills, with the ability to produce clear technical specifications, runbooks, and RFCs.


Ability to understand stakeholder needs, translate ambiguous requests into actionable technical requirements, and explain complex concepts to both executives and subject matter experts.


A proactive and autonomous working style, with the ability to prioritize effectively, challenge unsafe or low-value requests constructively, and communicate progress across time zones.


A strong sense of ownership, including the ability to validate solutions with users, monitor performance after deployment, and continuously iterate.


Preferred Qualifications:


Experience in cryptocurrency, blockchain, payments, or fintech, particularly within regulated or audit-focused environments.


Experience creating reusable agent skills, plugins, or shared prompt libraries for organizational use.


Familiarity with model gateways such as OpenRouter, LiteLLM, or Portkey, including key management, model routing, and fallback strategies.


Experience extending open-source coding agents such as OpenCode or Pi.


Awareness of emerging agent identity standards, including MCP enterprise-managed authentication and Okta Cross App Access.


Knowledge of context and retrieval engineering, including vector stores, agent memory, and permission-aware retrieval systems.


Background in machine learning engineering, including model evaluation, fine-tuning, and model routing.


Experience working with agent runtimes and sandbox environments such as Modal, n8n, or containerized infrastructure.


Public technical contributions, such as open-source tools, servers, technical articles, or presentations demonstrating experience with production AI agents.


Benefits


Remote-first work environment: Join a globally distributed workforce and work remotely.

Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke – vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.7. Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe.

Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance.

Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction.
Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début.
Le contexte 
 
La squad Productivity est au cœur de la transformation produit autour de la gestion des affaires contentieuses de bout en bout.
Le scope de la squad s'est considérablement enrichi, au-delà du seul gain de productivité, en allant vers l'accompagnement de la réflexion et de l'argumentation juridique, à travers plusieurs langues.
 
Aujourd’hui, elle est responsable de toute la chaîne de valeur :
1. Analyse de documents
2. Rédaction automatisée des conclusions et documents juridiques
3. Réflexion stratégique sur l’argumentation
 
C’est le cœur de notre IA appliquée au raisonnement juridique : travail avancé sur les modèles LLM, le machine learning et la structuration de documents complexes.1.
 
Tu peux trouver des détails sur l’ensemble de la stack sur Github !

Concevoir et développer des features produit de bout en bout — de la modélisation back-end à l'interface utilisateur, en ownership complet sur tes sujets.
Intégrer des modèles d'IA et LLM dans les flux produit — pour enrichir l'expérience des avocats et juristes qui utilisent Doctrine au quotidien.
Maintenir et faire évoluer notre architecture cloud — stack moderne, scalabilité, fiabilité des services en production.
Participer activement aux choix techniques de ta squad — revues de code, décisions d'architecture, amélioration continue de la qualité du code.
Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes Produit et Design — pour transformer des problèmes métier complexes en solutions techniques concrètes et utiles.
Contribuer à la roadmap technique transverse — outillage, dette technique, documentation, et montée en compétences collective.

Tu es autonome et orienté ownership — tu prends un sujet, tu le cadres, tu le livres. Tu n'attends pas qu'on te dise quoi faire.
Tu travailles bien avec le Produit — tu comprends le besoin utilisateur, tu sais challenger un spec, et tu penses impact avant technologie.
Tu as une appétence pour l'IA — tu n'es pas forcément expert LLM, mais tu t'y intéresses activement et tu vois comment ça transforme les produits.

Les à côtés du poste 👁
Comme tous les ingénieurs de Doctrine, tu participeras à un de nos chapters transverse, en l’espèce le chapter Web. Au sein de ce chapter, tu contribueras à des projets internes pour améliorer nos process et notre vision long-terme. Le chapter se réunit toutes les semaines pour :
🤝 Partager des connaissances : suivit de l’état de l’art, revue de papiers scientifiques, amélioration continue, bonnes pratiques,…
🎯 Proposer des évolutions : nouveaux outils à expérimenter, nouveaux process à mettre en œuvre

description_clean: Qui sommes-nous ?Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 6 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises.La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement.Nous recherchons une Post-doctorante ou un Post-doctorant en transmission et détection sur fibres à cœurs creux pour rejoindre le département COMELEC à Télécom Paris.Les fibres à cristaux photoniques à cœur creux (Hollow-Core Photonic Crystal Fibers, HCPCF) ont récemment franchi une étape technologique majeure, avec des pertes de propagation pouvant atteindre 0.1 dB/km à 1550 nm, comparables, voire inférieures, à celles des fibres télécoms standards [1–2]. La lumière se propageant principalement dans l’air, les HCPCF présentent une latence réduite de 30 à 40 %, une dispersion ultra-faible et des non-linéarités optiques négligeables. Ces propriétés uniques en font des technologies particulièrement prometteuses pour les systèmes de télécommunications de nouvelle génération, la distribution quantique de clés (Quantum Key Distribution, QKD) sur longue distance et les applications de détection distribuée.Le projet proposé vise à développer et démontrer la prochaine génération de fibres à cristaux photoniques à cœur creux (HCPCF) pour la transmission de données à haut débit et les applications de détection. La propagation de la lumière dans l’air plutôt que dans le verre permet aux HCPCF d’offrir une latence réduite et des non-linéarités optiques négligeables par rapport aux fibres de silice, répondant ainsi à certains des enjeux majeurs des futurs centres de données et réseaux optiques. Notre ambition est de démontrer une transmission à 400 Gbit/s sur quelques kilomètres à travers des échantillons de fibres issus de nouvelles architectures, et d’étudier le potentiel de ces HCPCF pour des applications de détection. La réalisation de ces objectifs nécessite de répondre à des spécifications exigeantes en matière de guidage monomode, de contrôle de la polarisation, ainsi que de faibles pertes par courbure et par couplage.Deux équipes complémentaires assureront conjointement l'encadrement de ces travaux : le GPPMM, reconnu internationalement pour ses activités de conception et de fabrication de HCPCF [3–5], et le GTO, leader dans la démonstration de systèmes de communication optique et de détection à haut débit [6–8]. Un processus itératif entre la fabrication des fibres et leur caractérisation au niveau système permettra de s'assurer que leurs propriétés répondent aux exigences opérationnelles en matière de transmission et de détection. Sur le plan méthodologique, le projet combinera modélisation numérique, caractérisation et validation expérimentale dans la bande C. Les méthodes de modélisation et de traitement du signal développées au GTO pour le suivi de la polarisation contribueront à évaluer et à optimiser les performances de transmission des HCPCF conçues et caractérisées au GPPMM.À propos du projet PLEIADESLe projet PLEIADES s'inscrit dans le cadre du programme PEPR « Réseaux du futur », financé par l'ANR, et réunit un consortium de 14 partenaires. L'un des axes de travail porte sur les fibres à cœur creux de nouvelle génération et rassemble plusieurs laboratoires académiques, notamment LTCI, XLIM et PHLAM.Vos principales missions seront de :Assurer des missions de recherche dans le domaine de la photoniqueAssurer des missions d’encadrement et de tutoratParticiper à la notoriété de l’Ecole, de l’Institut Mines-Télécom et de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris  Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat ou équivalent en génie électrique, communications, photonique, traitement du signal ou dans un domaine connexe. Vous disposez de solides connaissances en systèmes et réseaux de transmission optique ainsi qu’en traitement numérique du signal (DSP) appliqué aux systèmes de communication ou aux capteurs à fibre optique. La maîtrise de MATLAB et/ou Python pour le développement d’algorithmes DSP sera appréciée. description_clean: About RecareAs one of the leading German HealthTech companies, we are reshaping discharge management: technology-driven, patient-centered and free from bureaucracy. title: Senior People Partner
description_clean: Senior People PartnerCloudscaler | London | People Team | Reports to the Chief People Officer | £55,000–£75,000Someone has to own the People initiative that doesn’t fit neatly into anyone’s week and the case nobody else should be handling. That someone is you — not as an escalation point, but as the person who runs the day-to-day of this function.THE MOMENTCloudscaler is 130 people today. We’ll be 170 by the end of this year, and roughly double again in 2027. The People function is being built in real time alongside that growth, rather than inherited from someone who left years ago.You’ll be the first hire into the People team. For roughly your first year you’ll be the only People professional alongside the CPO, which means running the whole day-to-day of the function: the hardest casework and initiatives, and the operational core that keeps everything moving. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them.This is also a role built with room to grow. As the team expands beyond that second hire, we expect this role to take on day-to-day operational leadership of the People Partner practice, but that isn’t the shape of it on day one.WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENTIn most People teams, the senior generalist is just a People Partner with a harder case queue. Here, the difference is ownership, not just difficulty.Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back.People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding.Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning.CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to.To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one.THE ROLEYou’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job:Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish.Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs.Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate.When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day.WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPSNew roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today.YoursThe most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end.Full ownership of People initiatives, from design to embedding.Acting as the CPO’s operational partner on ambiguous or cross-cutting problems.Until the People Partner joins (planned for later in 2027):Payroll and benefits administration, including the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling and Mintago.Pre-onboarding, onboarding and probation.Background screening in Zinc.Security clearance coordination.Rippling data quality, workflows and reporting.Our working groups and committees.Once the People Partner joins:A structured handover of the operational core.Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner.SharedAshby, which Talent Acquisition owns. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on every hire until the People Partner joins, and on senior hires after that.Mentoring and supporting the People Partner on their casework and initiatives, once they join.Not yoursRecruitment delivery, which sits with Talent Acquisition.The design of the People strategy, the operating model and the systems architecture, which sit with the CPO.Formal line management of the People Partner, who will report to the CPO.THE STACKRippling: Our single source of truth. Until the People Partner joins you’ll run it day to day, including the monthly payroll cycle, data quality and workflows, and you’ll use its reporting at a level that supports whole initiatives.Zinc: Background screening. You’ll run checks for every new joiner until the People Partner joins, and stay close to the senior and sensitive hires after that.Ashby: Owned by Talent Acquisition. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on the hires you’re responsible for.Claude: A daily tool here. You’ll use it for casework preparation, drafting policy and communications, and pulling together the analysis behind an initiative.Mintago: Our employee benefits and financial wellbeing platform (pensions, salary sacrifice and financial advice). You’ll administer it and keep enrolment accurate until the People Partner takes it on.WHAT YOU’LL DOOwn the hardest casework. You’ll run our most complex and sensitive employee relations cases end to end, with the CPO there to sense-check rather than take over.Own initiatives, not tasks. You’ll take a People initiative from a rough brief to something that’s running and embedded, rather than handing it back once the interesting part is done.Run the operational core. Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling, benefits administration including Mintago, onboarding, background screening and security clearances. Accurate, on time, and documented as you go.Hand it over well. When the People Partner arrives, you’ll give them a working system and a clear handover, then stay the person they come to first and the judgement others in the function measure themselves against.Partner with senior leaders. You’ll be credible with leaders on the most difficult conversations: complex change, capability, and situations without a clean playbook.Use AI properly. You’ll use Claude daily to take time out of your own week, checking anything that touches a decision about a person and owning the outcome.Improve what you find. You’ll spot the gaps in policy, process or practice before anyone else does, and bring the CPO a considered view on the fix, not just the problem.WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT 12 MONTHSYou’re running the most complex ER cases with confidence, and the CPO isn’t being pulled into them.At least one or two People initiatives have gone from a rough brief to something genuinely embedded, owned by you.Payroll, benefits, onboarding and clearances run accurately and on time, and every process is documented well enough to hand over.You’ve helped shape the People Partner hire, so the handover is ready when they land.Senior leaders treat you as a credible operational partner, not an escalation point.You’ve made and documented sensible calls in genuinely ambiguous situations, and they’ve held up.The CPO can hand you an ambiguous problem and trust it gets shaped properly.WHO WE’RE LOOKING FORDeep employee relations experience. You’ve run complex disciplinaries, grievances and change situations yourself, and you know exactly when to escalate and when not to. CIPD qualification, or solid progress towards it, is welcome.A track record of owning initiatives. You can point to work you took from a brief to something that actually ran, not just a project you contributed to.Hands-on with the operational detail. You’ve owned or closely supported a payroll cycle, benefits administration and onboarding, and you’re comfortable being accountable for their accuracy while also carrying the senior work.Credible with senior leaders. You can hold your own in a difficult conversation with someone under real pressure and be listened to.Comfortable operating near-autonomously. You don’t need a playbook for everything. You make a sensible call, write it down, and check it with the CPO afterwards.Ready to grow into people leadership. You won’t formally manage anyone at the start, but you’ll induct and guide the People Partner when they join, and you should want to lead a team as the structure catches up.Discreet and organised at volume. Complex casework and live initiatives, often at the same time. You’ll need a system, and it can’t be your memory.THE HONEST PARTThis role sits in an odd space for now: senior in scope and judgement, without a team underneath it yet. Until the People Partner joins later in 2027, you’ll also be the whole operational team, so a payroll deadline and a complex grievance can land in the same week. That eases as the function grows, but it means the authority you carry day to day has to come from the quality of your work, not a job title.You are not designing the People strategy or the systems architecture. The CPO does that. What you get instead is real ownership of the hardest cases and the initiatives that matter, a close working relationship with the CPO, and a genuine path toward leading the People Partner practice as it grows.This probably isn’t for you if you want a formal team from day one, or if you’d rather leave payroll and onboarding to someone else. The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we're behind some of Spotify's most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you'll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.
Within Personalization, the Speak Team owns the development of Spotify's state-of-the-art speech models, contributing to speech recognition, speech synthesis, and speech-to-speech models. We craft voice models that match human-level emotional expressiveness, so we can deeply engage our listeners and support creators at scale. Our groundbreaking work on speech synthesis relies on state-of-the-art deep learning methods and evaluation techniques, highly efficient data processing and model serving, and capturing audio of outstanding quality from our voice talent pool.
We're looking for a senior applied research scientist with experience in developing novel ML techniques and architectures and with a strong interest in working across a full production pipeline to produce state-of-the-art generative conversational speech-to-speech models. You'll collaborate with our engineering teams to help develop our production pipelines, explore new ideas and methods to improve quality, understanding and realism, as well as push the frontiers of what is possible with our speech technology.
What You'll Do


Develop and experiment with new methods for speech synthesis and speech recognition, along with end-to-end approaches, building on the latest research and ideas.
Work towards the expansion of our speech use-cases targeting different markets and products.
Be part of a highly motivated research team dedicated to building and creating models at scale to power the Spotify platform.
Champion best practices for research and development, sharing your knowledge and experience with other researchers within Speak.
Collaborate with our engineering and data teams on ideas requiring new infrastructure or new high-quality data, as well as to help improve our speech recognition and speech synthesis pipelines, and help turn proven ideas into scalable products.


Who You Are


You have a strong background in ML (PhD degree on top of professional experience), and experience in working with any of the following: transformers, GANs, diffusion models, flow matching, VAEs, audio codecs.
You have experience in developing generative models for speech synthesis, speech recognition, audio/music, natural language processing, or computer vision.
You have strong experience with Python, particularly PyTorch.
You have strong communication skills and the ability to explain technical ideas with clarity to technical and non-technical people alike.
You have experience in an academic or professional setting conducting high-quality research.


Where You'll Be


This role is based in London or Stockholm.
We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home

title: Quadrants: Compiler Lead
description_clean: What Quadrants isQuadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research.The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton.It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public.The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast.The roleYou own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap.Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. Getting there is a frontier problem, part research and part engineering, and we intend to define the state of the art on it, relentlessly pushing the limit further.It calls for two things at once: the low-level GPU and compiler skill to make a single kernel optimal, and the ability to keep the whole system coherent as it grows.The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX.Your mandate is to build the best open-source Python compiler for physics simulation out there. Our global Security team aspires to be the world's most admired security team, with members across EU, UK and North America (operating as Wolt, Deliveroo and Doordash).
We're shaping our next generation infrastructure that is hardened from the ground up. This is a rare opportunity - no legacy tech or off-the-shelf product solutions. There is a lot to do around this new development as well as our "classic" platforms of the three companies.
The greater team is not just information security - we're more holistic, and also physical security and safety are a part of our global operations.

 
This position is open in our Wolt hubs in Berlin, Germany, or Helsinki, Finland, and will be a part of the Global Security Engineering team.
 
Day-to-day in this role you'll:
 

Build and maintain core security products, including but not limited to Remote Access Management, Secrets Management, Tokenization, Encryption and Knowledge Graphs, Access Control at global scale.
Partner cross-functionally with Core Infrastructure, Product Engineering, Legal, Security teams and Vendor Partners to build "paved paths" that provide actionable feedback to embed secure design practices into the product and infrastructure development process.
Lead the technical direction and roadmap for your assigned area of ownership.
Build and maintain high Operational Excellence (OE) to ensure we operate T0 services with excellence, rigor and durable standards to ensure minimal to no downtime.
Participate in on-call rotation and promptly respond to on-call events with urgency and rigor.
Manage the lifecycle of security product feature requests and improvements full life-cycle from triage, validation, design, testing, and implementation.
Influence and drive improvements to engineering standards, leverage advancements and LLMs to improve productivity and velocity.
Mentor and coach earlier career engineers, setting and enforcing high standards for Operational Excellence and Software Engineering.

 
Over time, your role can evolve depending on your interests and skills. Our company is  a large place and there's a lot to do!

Able to demonstrate a track record of driving improvements to a company's infrastructure security posture.
Breadth of technical experience across various infrastructure and security areas running in large production environments.
Highly skilled in distributed systems and platforms development using program languages such as Java/Scala/Kotlin, Golang, or Python.
Strong experience with infrastructure as a code tooling like Terraform.
Expertise with cloud infrastructure and management in AWS.
Experience solving complex, systemic issues that require creative thinking and solutions.
Exceptional analytical and investigative abilities with hands-on experience leading root cause analysis.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills to review design documents with respect to cloud infrastructure, security and engineering personnel.
Must be comfortable regularly exercising discretion and independent judgment in performing job duties, including evaluating options, making informed decisions, and determining appropriate courses of action within the scope of assigned responsibilities with minimal oversight.

title: Founding Strategy & Operations
description_clean: Alassio recherche son (sa) prochain(e) Founding Strategy & Operations !  Missions 🏗️ Alassio en quelques motsEn France, la paie et le social comptent parmi les fonctions les plus réglementées qui soient. Entre inflation réglementaire et évolutions légales et conventionnelles incessantes, la conformité est devenue un véritable fardeau pour les cabinets de paie et les services RH :ce fardeau les empêche de se consacrer à ce qui compte vraiment, le conseil et l'accompagnement des salariés, qui en subissent donc eux aussi le poids ;c'est aussi l'un des métiers où l'attrition est la plus forte en France, notamment parce que 60 % du temps des gestionnaires de paie est encore consacré à de la saisie ou à de la relecture manuelle.Pourtant, des solutions technologiques majeures existent : l'IA permet en particulier d'automatiser une très grande partie des tâches les plus pénibles et de valoriser les données sociales. Mais le secteur reste largement à l'écart de cette révolution, et le problème n'est pas seulement réglementaire : le marché était verrouillé par des éditeurs historiques vieillissants, difficiles à quitter faute d'alternative crédible et de moyens pour migrer efficacement. Là aussi, l'IA fait voler ces barrières en éclats et ouvre la voie à une vague d'innovation attendue depuis des décennies.C'est pour y répondre qu'Alassio construit la plateforme de paie et de gestion RH moderne qui manquait à ce marché, au service des cabinets et de leurs clients TPE/PME. Notre ambition est de développer en un temps record :une plateforme collaborative et ouverte, qui s'intègre nativement aux outils des cabinets et de leurs clients, respecte leurs habitudes de travail et fluidifie les échanges entre gestionnaires de paie et entreprises ;l'automatisation de la tenue administrative : collecte des données, paramétrage des évolutions légales et des règles propres à chaque entreprise, génération automatique des rapports et formulaires, traçabilité juridique dynamique et en temps réel, etc. ;la valorisation des données de paie et sociales, pour offrir un conseil social à 360° et enfin répondre efficacement à l'ensemble des attentes des salariés, qui se sont de surcroît largement amplifiées depuis le Covid : gestion contractuelle, pilotage de la masse salariale, avantages salariés, fidélisation des talents, mutuelle…L'objectif : devenir le « People OS » sur lequel les cabinets et leurs clients TPE/PME s'appuient pour gérer l'intégralité de leurs problématiques paie et RH. 🚀 Tes responsabilitésTa mission est de concevoir et faire vivre les systèmes de fonctionnement d'Alassio. NaroIQ gives ManCos a fast, reliable path into the ETF market. We provide the digital ETF infrastructure that reduces operational complexity, so ManCos can launch and run ETFs at scale and compete effectively, helping broaden access to the market beyond dominant, US-based providers.
We are remote-first, with in-person collaboration opportunities. We work with international clients and have raised over $10m from top-tier investors and operators across finance and technology.

You own the two functions that decide how the outside world experiences NaroIQ: How we are perceived in the market, and who we manage to attract to build it. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works.You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.— GrigoryWhy Secfix existsOver 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.What you'll actually do in the first 3 monthsThis isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. title: Senior Software Engineer, Inference Performance
description_clean:
About Tensordyne 
AI is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications.Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence!
The role
You'll build the software stack that takes a model from code down to the hardware: the abstractions, kernels, libraries, and tools that engineers and agents use to reach peak performance. Help optimize the latest AI models on our silicon.
Our hardware is designed to be straightforward to program, so the goal is not to hide it. The goal is to expose the right level of control at each layer, from our compiler-driven Python SDK to our low-level Rust programming stack, and to make every performance gap measurable and every fix permanent.
We're looking for a builder who understands hardware deeply and develops with agents by default. You'll own substantial parts of one of these layers and work closely with engineers across models, compilers, runtime, and hardware. Your focus is performance: where cycles, bandwidth, and communication go, and how to win them back. Number formats and model accuracy are owned by our conversion and emulation team; you'll partner with them where precision and speed meet.

Build the stack. Design APIs, kernel abstractions, and libraries in our Python SDK or Rust stack so model engineers and agents can reach high performance at the layer that fits their problem.
Make models fast. Take priority workloads, from LLMs to multimodal models, to peak performance on real silicon. Profile, find the bottleneck across kernels, compiler, runtime, and parallelism, and fix it at the right layer.

Build the agentic performance loop. Give agents the profilers, traces, counters, and benchmark harnesses to form a hypothesis, change code, and measure the result in minutes. Make the results trustworthy enough to act on.
Set the bar for performance. Define how we measure, track regressions, and report results.
Build for the next chip. Design abstractions that carry forward to future hardware generations. Work with hardware architects to test how architectural choices affect real workloads.

What we need from you

You understand hardware performance. You've optimized AI workloads on GPUs or custom accelerators and can reason about compute utilization, memory hierarchy, latency hiding, synchronization, and multi-chip scaling.
You build excellent software. You've owned substantial systems from design through production. You're strong in Python and/or at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or C, and rigorous about interfaces, abstractions, and testing. We care about engineering quality more than a specific language.
You understand LLM inference end to end. You can read a new model's implementation and reason about prefill, decode, attention variants, KV caches, MoE, and parallelism, and how they map to compute, memory, and communication.
You build with agents. Agentic development is how you work, not an experiment. You'd rather build the loop that finds the optimization than find it by hand, and you know when the loop still needs a human.
You build things others succeed with. You've designed APIs, libraries, or performance tooling that other engineers adopted.
You drive problems to resolution. You form clear hypotheses, measure, and follow the evidence across software and hardware boundaries. You take ownership of the result.

Experience with embedded, bare-metal, or low-level runtime programming.

Contributions to LLM serving stacks such as vLLM or SGLang, or a track record of taking end-to-end inference workloads to competitive performance on a hardware target.

Your code will decide how fast models run on our hardware, and how easy it is for the next engineer, or the next agent, to make them faster. title: UI Engineer (Based in CA or NC only)
description_clean: Mission: Live at the intersection of app runtime & security. BlueRock is changing the landscape of App runtime security.The roleLocation: Must be based in CA (preferably San Francisco Bay Area) or North CarolinaYou will work alongside BlueRock's product designers and the control plane development team on our operator consoles. These are the React front ends that engineers and security teams use to manage large fleets of protected nodes, see what AI agents are actually doing across those fleets, and author the policy that constrains them.The domain is AI and agentic systems, seen from the operations and security side. When an agent calls an MCP server, spawns a subagent, runs a shell command in a sandbox, or burns $40 of tokens in an afternoon, our UI is where a person sees it, understands it, and decides what to allow. So the interesting problems are visibility problems (how do you show a thousand agent sessions so someone can find the one that matters?) and control problems (how do you author an enforcement policy without a mistake taking production down?).This is a mid-level role. We expect about 3–5 years of professional front-end experience, or equivalent work that clearly shows the same judgment. The ideal candidate is passionate about user experience, design, and AI-assisted software development, with a demonstrated grounding in engineering best practices. The title says UI, but the work doesn’t stop there: you’ll work closely with our backend services, and a feature is finished when it’s proven working live, not when the screen looks right.Working with design delivered as codeAt BlueRock, product designers design and collaborate in code. Instead of handing off static mockups, they build working UI with AI coding tools, against real data, and open merge requests. Iteration happens so quickly that it has outpaced our capacity for robust engineering collaboration and review.This role closes that gap. You will collaborate directly with product designers and backend developers to keep UI development fast, by bridging the gap between vibe code and high-quality, sustainable, well-tested code. Some days that means reviewing and hardening a designer's branch so it can merge. Other days it means building the shared components, tests and guardrails that make the next branch need less hardening.Beyond reviewing and hardening code, you'll help shape how it gets made. Working with designers and the AI tools they use, you'll turn what each review teaches us into shared components, conventions, tests and agent instructions. Over time the whole practice becomes more predictable, and each new branch arrives closer to production-ready.Roles and collaborationSoftware development roles are blurring more than ever. This role reports to product design, with API and data-layer guidance from our control plane engineering lead. You must be attuned to the perspectives of both UX/Design and Engineering, acting as a bridge between the goals and priorities of both sides, while ultimately deferring to UX/design partners on matters of style, copy, and information architecture.In practice: when a designer's branch makes a choice about layout, copy or flow, you protect the intent and fix the implementation. When the implementation can't support the intent, because of performance, data shape or maintainability, you say so early and bring options rather than quietly changing the design.What you'll doReview designer-authored merge requests and bring them to production quality: structure, types, tests, accessibility, performance, and both light and dark themes.Turn one-off UI from fast iteration into shared, documented components in our design system and Storybook, and migrate the apps onto them.Make data-dense views hold up at real scale. Dashboards, tables, charts, and time-range and filter controls that work on a demo tenant also have to work on one with billions of events.Wire UI to the API layer (GraphQL), and work with backend developers when a view needs a new query, field or endpoint.Own UI test coverage: Vitest for units and Playwright for end-to-end flows, kept green in CI.Test UI end to end in live, secured environments, with full authentication and authorization, real data and realistic load, before calling it done.Keep UI work moving across release lines: shipping behind feature flags, and carrying fixes between branches when a release is frozen.Fix UI bugs across the consoles and the Windows, Mac and Linux clients: layout and overflow, tooltips and popovers, empty and zero states, things that are technically correct and still confusing.When needed, design new interfaces within the existing design system, and bring them to design for review.Help set the guardrails that make AI-assisted UI development safe: lint rules, conventions, review checklists, and the instructions our AI coding tools follow.How we expect you to workThese are the habits of a careful engineer. They matter more here, not less, because so much of the code you touch was drafted quickly by someone else or by an AI tool.Diagnose before you change. Find the actual cause, which is usually a layer away from the symptom, and be able to explain why your fix addresses it. A change that makes the symptom disappear is not the same as a fix.Small, deliberate diffs. Solve the problem in front of you. Don't refactor adjacent code on the way past, and don't build the abstraction you may need later.Fix it in one place. When the same bug shows up in three panels, the fix belongs in the shared component, not copied three times. Knowing where a change belongs is most of the skill.Verify, then claim. Run it, look at it, check both themes and a narrow viewport, get types and lint clean, and write the test where a test is what proves it. Then say plainly what you checked and what you did not. This applies double to AI-assisted work: you own the diff, whoever drafted it.Say when you're unsure. A requirement with two readings is a question, not a guess. Surfacing a problem early is always cheaper than discovering it in review.Our UI stack and design systemOur front ends are several React and TypeScript apps that share one codebase: our enterprise operator consoles and our cloud product for builders.All of them are built on our own design system. It is a shared React component library on top of Ant Design, with design tokens for color, type and spacing, light and dark themes, and a shared app shell for navigation, page layout and headers. Every component is documented in Storybook, published from CI, which serves as the reference for designers, engineers and AI coding tools alike. The library also carries written instructions for AI coding assistants, so generated code reaches for the system's components and tokens instead of inventing its own.A large part of this role is the design system itself. That means promoting patterns out of individual apps into shared components, writing their stories, keeping tokens and themes consistent so the apps don't drift, and making the system the easiest path for anyone, or any agent, building UI.Front end: React, TypeScript, ViteDesign system: our component library built on Ant Design, including design tokens and light and dark themesDocumentation: Storybook, published to GitLab PagesData and charts: GraphQL; ECharts for the data-dense viewsTesting: Vitest, Playwright, and contract and smoke suites in CIDelivery: GitLab merge requests and pipelines, release branches, feature flagsFurther back: TypeScript and Rust services over graph and columnar stores, built on OpenTelemetry, plus desktop apps and services across Mac, Windows and LinuxYou don't need experience with all of it. You do need to be strong in TypeScript and React, and willing to read code before changing it.What you bringAbout 3–5 years building production front ends in TypeScript and modern React: hooks, composition, state that lives at the right level, and an understanding of why a re-render happens.An end-to-end view of the systems behind the UI. Designing in code gets a feature most of the way to working, and you close the rest of the gap. For you, “done” doesn’t stop at the UI working. It means the UI is integrated and shown to work live, in a secured environment with full authentication and authorization, under realistic load.Integration testing against complex backends. Tests that only run against mock data in a standalone dev stack aren’t enough here. You can create, integrate and run tests in live environments to check data validity, load, security and scale, and you keep unit, integration and end-to-end suites green in CI.Performance instincts for data-heavy UI: pagination, virtualization, server-side filtering, and knowing when a slow page is a query problem rather than a rendering problem.A track record of reviewing other people’s code and improving it without rewriting it.Git in complex repositories with several active release branches, where a single fix may need to be cherry-picked, ported or graft-merged onto more than one of them. Readable commits, and responding to review without taking it personally.Hands-on use of AI coding tools in real work, with clear habits for checking what they produce.CSS that holds up: flexbox and grid, overflow and scroll containers, responsive behaviour, and why a tooltip or popover ends up clipped.Experience building or contributing to a component library or design system, ideally with Storybook and design tokens.Careful attention to visual detail and real interest in UX. Much of this work is noticing that something is two pixels wrong, or that a label is technically correct and still confusing.Genuine interest in the AI and agentic space, and in the operational and security questions it creates.Nice to have: Ant Design; GraphQL; ECharts or other charting libraries; design training or a portfolio; experience on a team where designers commit code; writing conventions or instructions for AI coding tools; desktop UI across Mac, Windows and Linux; dense operational tooling such as observability, security or infrastructure products.Not required: a computer science degree, if your work shows the same rigor. Deep backend, security or infrastructure expertise, or any knowledge of our domain (fleet management, telemetry, agent observability, policy enforcement). We will teach that.Your first 90 daysFirst month: land changes safely. Ship scoped fixes in the consoles. Learn the component library, theme tokens and API layer. Start reviewing designer merge requests alongside an engineer.Second month: own review on a surface. Become the primary reviewer for designer-authored UI on one product area, and extract at least one repeated pattern into a shared component.Third month: make the next branch easier. Get the flows you own covered by tests in CI, and write down the conventions and guardrails that make designer branches need less hardening.About BlueRock:BlueRock is a well-funded, early stage cybersecurity company founded by experienced security minded entrepreneurs. BlueRock changes the game, enabling organizations to shift from chasing CVEs and exploits to proactively protecting the foundations of applications and computing, so that developers can build great applications without looking over their shoulders.Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

Service mit Haltung. Du hast einen starken Dienstleistungsgedanken und dich stört es nicht, zu unterschiedlichen Tageszeiten sowie in geregelten Abständen am Wochenende im Dienst zu sein.

Als innovativer Hybrid aus Social Media Publisher und Social Media Agentur vereint das VS Mediahouse einzigartige Expertise in den Bereichen Content-Kreation, Markenaufbau und Performance-Marketing. Mit einem Team von über 50 Experten in Social Media, Design und Videoproduktion betreiben wir die beliebtesten Social-Media-Marken Deutschlands auf Facebook, Instagram und TikTok. Unser tiefes Verständnis für die Dynamik von Social Media und unser Publishing-Know-how ermöglichen es uns, Marken wie Samsung, Schwartau, Bayer und Lexware im Bereich Social Media nachhaltig erfolgreich zu machen. Wir schaffen Verbindungen, erzählen Geschichten und setzen Trends – für echte Wirkung und messbaren Erfolg.Deine MissionDu beherrschst klassisches SEO in der Tiefe, mit mehrjähriger Senior-Erfahrung. Gleichzeitig ist dir klar: Kaum noch jemand sucht heute komplett ohne KI, sei es über ChatGPT, Gemini oder AI Overviews. Diesen Wandel willst du nicht nur beobachten, sondern aktiv gestalten. Klar ist dabei: Ohne solides SEO-Fundament funktioniert auch die beste GEO-Strategie nicht, deshalb bringst du beides mit.Als Head of SEO & AI Search verantwortest du unseren SEO-Bereich strategisch, operativ und wirtschaftlich. Im Zentrum deiner Rolle stehen von Beginn an unsere größten und strategisch wichtigsten Bestandskunden: Hier baust du die SEO- und AI-Search-Strategie neu und mit voller Verantwortung auf Senior-Ebene auf, im direkten Austausch mit der Geschäftsführung des Kunden. Perspektivisch entwickelst du von dort aus den SEO-Bereich für weitere Kunden im Haus.KI spielt dabei eine doppelte Rolle: erstens als Zielsystem, du machst Kunden auch in KI-gestützten Suchsystemen sichtbar. Zweitens als Arbeitsweise, du nutzt KI selbst für Recherche, Analysen, Briefings und Reporting. Ein fertiges Technik-Portfolio brauchst du dafür nicht, wichtiger sind echte Neugier und Lust, dich reinzuhängen. Bei uns wirst du zum KI-Poweruser deines Fachbereichs.Was erwartet dichAI Search & Sichtbarkeit – der Kern der Rolle, kein Nebenschauplatz: Du entwickelst Strategien, damit Inhalte in Google AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Gemini und Perplexity auffindbar, verständlich und zitierfähig sind. Du übernimmst die strategische, operative und wirtschaftliche Führung des SEO- und AI-Search-Mandats für einen unserer wichtigsten Kunden, von der Analyse bis zur Erfolgskontrolle. Du baust eine SEO- und GEO-Roadmap auf, die es in dieser Form bislang nicht gab, und verantwortest ihre Umsetzung.Beratung auf Augenhöhe: Du berätst die Geschäftsführung des Kunden souverän in Workshops, Audits und Reviews.Dein Alltag: KI als deine tägliche ArbeitsweiseHier geht es nicht um die Arbeit für Kunden, sondern um deinen eigenen Alltag: Viele wiederkehrende Aufgaben erledigst du bei uns spürbar schneller, weil du KI dafür einsetzt – kein Kür-Thema, sondern Standard. Die technischen Hürden legen wir bewusst niedrig, ein bisschen eigene Praxis braucht es trotzdem.Mehrjährige SEO- und AI-Search-Erfahrung aus Agentur- oder vergleichbarer Unternehmensumgebung, mit nachweisbaren Ergebnissen. Du hast bereits eigene Erfahrung mit KI-Tools gesammelt, und sei es nur privat (Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity & Co.). Ein Zertifikat oder eine Ausbildung brauchst du dafür nicht, wichtiger ist Lust, das jetzt systematisch für deine SEO-Arbeit einzusetzen.Denken in Leads, Conversions und Kundennutzen statt nur in Rankings, dazu eine eigenständige und strukturierte Arbeitsweise.Verhandlungssicheres Deutsch und sicheres Englisch.Warum VS MediahouseWir sind auf der Suche nach motivierten Mitarbeitenden, die etwas bewegen möchten, Mut für neue Ideen haben und das Unternehmen aktiv mitgestalten wollen. Wir legen großen Wert auf einen respektvollen Umgang auf Augenhöhe. Neben unseren modernen Büros im Herzen von Freiburg erwarten dich ausgezeichnete Arbeitsbedingungen in einem hoch dynamischen und wachstumsstarken Umfeld. Freue dich auf vielseitige Aufgaben mit hoher Eigenverantwortung und unternehmerischem Gestaltungsspielraum sowie eine moderne, sachorientierte Entscheidungskultur ohne unnötige Hierarchien. Wir bieten dir fachliche und persönliche Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten durch Freiraum für Innovationen, kurze Entscheidungswege und individuelles Management-Coaching.Das bieten wir dirWähle zwischen einem kostenfreien Jobticket (Deutschlandticket) oder nutze unser attraktives JobRad-Angebot.Um dich fit und gesund zu halten, subventionieren wir deine Hansefit-Mitgliedschaft.Du findest bei uns modernste Ausstattung mit höhenverstellbaren Schreibtischen sowie Macbook & iPhone (auch zur privaten Nutzung) und natürlich ist das Arbeiten aus dem Homeoffice auch für uns kein Fremdwort.Für Zwischendurch bedienst du dich an unserem regionalen Obst, Müsli, Kaffee, Getränke und vieles mehr.Neben deinem persönlichen Corporate Benefits Zugang erhältst du 50% Rabatt auf unsere Produkte in unserem Shop.Erweitere deine Rente durch die Teilnahme an der betrieblichen Altersvorsorge.Abgerundet wird deine Zeit bei uns natürlich auch mit verschiedenen Team-Events und Feiern.Klingt nach dir?Wir suchen niemanden, der nur Rankings reportet, und genauso wenig einen reinen KI-Enthusiasten ohne SEO-Substanz. Sondern jemanden, der SEO in der Tiefe beherrscht, Lust hat, KI in den eigenen Arbeitsalltag zu integrieren, und bereit ist, für einen unserer wichtigsten Kunden von Anfang an echte Verantwortung zu übernehmen. Technisches KI-Vorwissen ist zweitrangig, echte Motivation nicht.Ein Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht. Beschreibe uns stattdessen kurz zwei bis drei SEO-Projekte, für die du verantwortlich warst (Ausgangslage, deine Rolle, Ergebnis), und beantworte:1. Wie nutzt du KI heute schon in deinem Alltag, und was reizt dich daran, KI-gestützte Suche zum Kernteil deiner Arbeit zu machen?2. Wo hast du KI schon sinnvoll in einem SEO-Prozess eingesetzt? Falls noch nicht: Was würdest du als Erstes ausprobieren?3. Wie misst du SEO-Erfolg, wenn Rankings und Klicks allein nicht mehr reichen?Wenn du mehr über unsere Arbeitskultur und das Arbeitsumfeld erfahren möchtest, laden wir dich ein, die Bewertungen unserer Mitarbeiter auf Kununu zu lesen. Dort findest du ehrliche Meinungen und Feedback von aktuellen und ehemaligen Mitarbeitern.Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Manager Business Development mit Schwerpunkt Projektakquise (m/w/d) im Bereich Erneuerbare Energien
description_clean:
Was wir tun"Eine enkeltaugliche Welt hinterlassen"
Mit dieser Zielsetzung hat sich VISPIRON ENERGY eine strategische Position im Zukunftsmarkt der erneuerbaren Energien erarbeitet. Das ursprünglich auf Photovoltaikparks spezialisierte Unternehmen legte im Jahr 2017 den Fokus auf die Vernetzung regenerativer Energiesysteme und konzipierte das Ökosystem ENERGY WORLD. Regenerative Energieerzeuger, Verbraucher, Speicher und Hochleistungsladesäulen werden in diesem Ökosystem vernetzt und intelligent bewirtschaftet. Wir decken die Wertschöpfungskette von der Projektstrukturierung über den Anlagenbau bis hin zur Energievermarktung, zum Kapazitätshandel und zur Betriebsführung ab.
Hierzu arbeiten die hochspezialisierten Unternehmen VISPIRON ENERGY, VISPIRON EPC und SEtrade als Einheit zusammen und decken die Wertschöpfungskette von der Projektstrukturierung über den Anlagenbau bis hin zur Energievermarktung, zum Kapazitätshandel und zur Betriebsführung ab.
Sind wir ein Match?
Du

hast Freude daran, neue Geschäftsmöglichkeiten zu erschließen, Menschen für gemeinsame Projekte zu begeistern und nachhaltiges Wachstum aktiv mitzugestalten.
erkennst Chancen und Potenziale für neue Energieprojekte, bevor andere sie sehen.
gehst aktiv auf Flächeneigentümer, Kommunen, Unternehmen und Projektpartner zu und baust langfristige Beziehungen auf.
verhandelst souverän und findest Lösungen, die für alle Beteiligten Mehrwert schaffen.
arbeitest eigenverantwortlich, strukturiert und behältst auch bei komplexen Verhandlungen den Überblick.
verstehst, dass erfolgreiche Projektakquise Vertrieb, Verhandlung und Beziehungsmanagement gleichermaßen bedeutet.
möchtest einen direkten Beitrag zur Energiewende leisten und die Grundlage für neue Energieprojekte schaffen.

Wir

Wir arbeiten seit 20 Jahren täglich daran, die Abhängigkeit von fossilen Energieträgern zu beenden.
Wir wollen eine enkeltaugliche Welt hinterlassen.
Wir glauben an das Potential unserer Mitarbeiter:innen.
Wir sind Pioniere und haben neue Technologien entwickelt.
Wir sind neugierig, leben eine offene Fehlerkultur und teilen unser Wissen.
Wir setzen innovative Geschäftsmodelle nachhaltig um.

Aufgaben
Job Results - Tätigkeiten

Generierung und Qualifizierung von Leads zur Sicherung attraktiver Flächen für Charge Farms, Energieparks und Batteriespeicherprojekte.
Identifikation und Bewertung neuer Projektpotenziale im Bereich Photovoltaik, Batteriespeicher und Ladeinfrastruktur.
Aufbau eines belastbaren Netzwerks aus Flächeneigentümern, Kommunen, Unternehmen und Projektpartnern zur langfristigen Sicherung neuer Projektmöglichkeiten.
Sicherung attraktiver Projektflächen durch den erfolgreichen Abschluss von Nutzungs- und Gestattungsverträgen.
Anbahnung und Abschluss von Kooperationsvereinbarungen zur Sicherung von Projektrechten und zur Erschließung neuer Geschäftsmöglichkeiten.
Entwicklung neuer Konzepte zur Erweiterung der Projektpipeline.
Pflege und Ausbau eines belastbaren Netzwerks aus Flächeneigentümern, Projektpartnern und Branchenkontakten.

Qualifikation
Deine Kompetenzen
Background: Abgeschlossene Ausbildung oder Studium, wünschenswert im Bereich Erneuerbare Energien. Wichtiger aber als dein Ausbildungsweg sind für uns deine Erfahrungen in der Akquise, dein Verhandlungsgeschick und dein unternehmerisches Denken.
Berufserfahrung: Mindestens 3–5 Jahre Erfahrung in der Projektakquise, Projektentwicklung, Flächensicherung, Immobilienentwicklung, Geschäftsentwicklung oder im Vertrieb komplexer Infrastruktur-, Energie- oder Immobilienprojekte.
Verhandlungsgeschick: Erfahrung in der Verhandlung von Nutzungsverträgen, Gestattungsverträgen, Kooperationsvereinbarungen oder vergleichbaren Vertragswerken.
Marktverständnis: Verständnis der wirtschaftlichen, regulatorischen und technischen Rahmenbedingungen von Photovoltaik-, Batteriespeicher- und Ladeinfrastrukturprojekten sowie der Anforderungen an eine erfolgreiche Projektentwicklung.
Netzwerkaufbau: Freude an der Ansprache neuer Kontakte und Fähigkeit, langfristige Beziehungen zu Flächeneigentümern, Kommunen, Unternehmen und Projektpartnern aufzubauen.
Kommunikation: Sicheres Auftreten gegenüber Eigentümern, Partnern, Behörden und weiteren Stakeholdern.
Eigeninitiative & Verantwortungsbewusstsein: Du arbeitest selbstständig, lösungsorientiert und bringst Themen konsequent zum Abschluss.
Sprachkenntnisse: Verhandlungssicheres Deutsch in Wort und Schrift.
Benefits
Was wir dir bieten

Wirkung: Du trägst aktiv dazu bei, dass neue Charge Farms, Energieparks und Batteriespeicherprojekte wie unser Energiepark Egling Realität werden – und damit zur Energiewende und zu einer enkeltauglichen Zukunft.
Team & Kultur: Sei du selbst und wachse mit uns (Wissenstransfer). Du wirst von einem freundlichen und leistungsstarken Team aus Energieexpertinnen und Experten mit langjähriger Unternehmenszugehörigkeit herzlich empfangen, die ihr tiefes akademisches und praktisches Wissen gerne teilen.
Fort-und Weiterbildung: Wir bieten interessante Entwicklungsperspektiven und ermöglichen aufgabenspezifische Fortbildungs- und Schulungsmöglichkeiten.
Arbeitsumfeld: Wir pflegen eine offene Arbeitskultur, in der Ideen und Initiativen gefördert werden. Zudem sind die Arbeitszeiten flexibel und basieren auf Vertrauen. Du erhältst ein hohes Maß an Eigenverantwortung und Gestaltungsspielraum beim Aufbau und der Entwicklung deiner Projektpipeline.
Entlohnung: Alle Mitarbeiter:innen sind gemeinsam am Unternehmenserfolg beteiligt. Weitere Benefits sind Zuschüsse zum Mittagessen in Firmenkantine, JobRad, Carsharing, betriebsinterne Kita, kostenlose Getränke und Obst, vegetarisches Essen und Sportangebote.
Standort: Unser Büro befindet sich in München und ist öffentlich gut erreichbar.

Warum brauchen wir dich im Team?
Unsere Projektakquise ist der Ausgangspunkt unserer gesamten Wertschöpfungskette. Hier entstehen die Projekte, die später entwickelt, finanziert, gebaut und betrieben werden.
Als Manager Business Development (m/w/d) identifizierst du neue Potenziale, erschließt neue Geschäftsmöglichkeiten, gewinnst Flächeneigentümer, Unternehmen, Kommunen und Projektpartner für gemeinsame Vorhaben und sicherst die Projektrechte für zukünftige Energieprojekte.
Du baust Netzwerke auf, verhandelst auf Augenhöhe mit unterschiedlichsten Stakeholdern und schaffst die Grundlage für die Energieinfrastruktur von morgen.
Dabei verbindest du unternehmerisches Denken mit Umsetzungsstärke und leistest einen wesentlichen Beitrag zum Wachstum unserer ENERGY WORLD.
Wenn du Freude daran hast, Chancen zu erkennen, Menschen zu begeistern und Projekte von Anfang an auf den Weg zu bringen, wirst du in dieser Rolle maßgeblich zum Erfolg unserer Mission beitragen:

description_clean: 📍 Manchester, UK (Hybrid 1 day WFH) | 💰 £50,000 - £55,000Street Group is a fast moving B2B SaaS business - grown in Manchester but on a UK wide mission to make moving house as easy as buying a car. We’ve recently raised strategic growth investment, and are scaling fast toward an ambitious growth plan - and we’re looking for an experienced Executive Assistant to support our Co-CEOs, so they can spend their time on growing the business.This is an opportunity for someone to join a scaling business during one of our most exciting chapters yet, and to build close relationships with Founders who both value and reward excellence.If you are organised, trustworthy, and dependable, and know what separates exceptional EAs from good ones - we think you might do great work here.How you’ll make a differenceYou make sure the Co-CEOs are spending their time on things that only they can do. You run their diaries and inboxes, delegate work where possible, and say no to people when a day is already full.You’ll make sure meetings with them are worth having - e.g. there's a defined agendas, people turn up prepared, and actions get followed up on. Before board and investor meetings, you’ll make sure they know the numbers and what’s in the board pack.Who we’re looking forYou’re an experienced EA, have worked with a CEO or founder before and understand the appropriate level of support for stakeholders at this level.You’re super organised, and can juggle requests coming in from multiple people with different ways of working.You’re trustworthy and reliable.You have exceptional attention to detail.You can build good relationships with people, and are able to say no to protect the founder’s diaries without souring relationships.Bonus points if you’re comfortable using AI tools - but it won’t rule you out!Why you might not want to applyWe'd rather be honest up front, because this role won't be for everyone.If you'd rather work for one person. You'll be balancing two founders' priorities, plus travel for our senior leaders - so you’ll be juggling different requirements and ways of working. If you want to work mostly from home. This role is 4 days a week in our Manchester office, so you're on hand when people need you.If that sounds like your kind of role, please apply and let us know why!Who are Street Group?We’re an award-winning PropTech business based in Manchester, founded in 2015 by brother and sister duo, Tom & Heather Staff.
